title: World Book Day
passage:
World Book Day is on 23 April every year. It's a day for people to show their love of books and reading. Children celebrate it in many fun ways. They sit down and read their favourite books, dress up as book characters, act out their favourite stories, paint pictures for books, and make bookmarks for family and friends. All the activities make reading more interesting.
World Book Day was started by UNESCO to encourage people, especially children, to open a book every day. Many schools hold a reading week, a book swap market, or a reading corner on that day. Children may dress up as their favourite character, such as Harry Potter or a pirate, and walk in a parade. Some libraries give every child a small book as a gift. The day reminds us that books are free friends who teach us about the world without leaving our seat.
passageZh:
世界读书日在每年4月23日，是人们表达对书籍和阅读之爱的日子。孩子们用许多有趣方式庆祝：读最喜欢的书、装扮成书中角色、表演最喜欢的故事、为书画画、为亲友做书签。所有活动让阅读更有趣。
世界读书日由联合国教科文组织发起，鼓励人们尤其是孩子每天翻开一本书。许多学校在这一天举办阅读周、旧书交换市场或阅读角。孩子们可以装扮成最喜欢的角色，如哈利·波特或海盗，参加游行。一些图书馆还给每个孩子送一本小书作礼物。这一天提醒我们：书是免费的朋友，不用离开座位就能教我们认识世界。
source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U3测试卷笔试（基础卷·阅读选择）

title: The Secret Garden
passage:
The Secret Garden is a great book by Frances Hodgson Burnett. Mary, a 10-year-old girl, lost her parents and lived with her uncle. She was unhappy and often angry at first. Then she found a secret garden and met Dickon. They worked together to make the garden alive. Mary became friendly and kind, and she also helped her cousin Colin get well. This book is about friends and love, and it shows the power of nature.
Mary moved to the big old house after her parents died of illness in India. At first she was a difficult, lonely child who spoke to no one. One morning she found a hidden garden behind a high wall, locked for years. With Dickon, a kind boy who knew plants, she cleared the grass and planted roses. As the garden bloomed, Mary bloomed too: she became cheerful, polite and caring. The garden also helped her sick cousin Colin stand up and walk again. The Secret Garden shows how nature and friendship can heal a sad heart.
passageZh:
《秘密花园》是弗朗西丝·霍奇森·伯内特写的好书。10岁女孩玛丽失去父母，和叔叔住一起，起初不开心、常生气。后来她发现秘密花园，遇见迪肯，一起让花园恢复生机。玛丽变得友善善良，还帮表弟科林康复。这本书讲友谊与爱，也展现自然的力量。
玛丽父母在印度病逝后，她搬到这座又大又旧的房子。起初她孤僻难相处，不和人说话。一天早晨她在高墙后发现一座紧锁多年的秘密花园。她和懂植物的善良男孩迪肯一起除草、种玫瑰。花园绽放时玛丽也变得开朗、有礼、体贴。花园还帮助生病的表弟科林重新站起来走路。《秘密花园》展现自然与友谊如何治愈一颗悲伤的心。

title: The horse library
passage:
The horse library is a special library. It comes every week, rain or shine. When Mum was young, her library only came once a month. It was a small library with not many books, but Mum loved it. Books gave her a lot of fun. Today, the horse library brings not only books but also joy to us.
A horse library usually rides out to villages that have no bookshop on the road. The librarian puts books in two big bags on the horse's back and brings them to different houses every week. Children wait by the road with their reading cards, choose a book, and return the old one. Long ago, Mum also borrowed books from this kind of mobile library when she was a little girl. Now she takes her own child to it, and that passing on of joy is the magic of reading.

title: Sam and the street library
passage:
Sam loves reading and he often goes to the street library near his home. The street library is small but nice. There are many types of books there, like history books, adventure fiction and fantasy stories. Last weekend, Sam read a history book about the Chinese nation there. He wrote a book report after reading it. He said the street library brings him a lot of fun and he can learn a lot from books.
The street library is a small wooden box on the sidewalk where people leave books for others to take. Anyone can borrow a book for free and put it back when finished. Sam visits it every Saturday afternoon. He likes to share what he reads with his classmates, and he often leaves a short note inside the book for the next reader. He believes that sharing a book is like sharing a piece of knowledge, and it makes reading a kind of friendship between strangers.

title: Why learn history?
passage:
Learning history is very important for us. We can learn about the things from the past, like ancient food, old buildings and great events. We know how people lived a long time ago and how our country developed. We can also learn the spirit of great people, like Fan Jinshi who protected history, and the Red Army who had the never-give-up spirit. History tells us many great lessons, and it helps us to live a better life today.
History is all around us, not only in textbooks. The old bridge in our town, the noodles our grandfathers ate, and the festivals we still celebrate all carry history. Studying the past helps us understand why our country looks the way it does, and why people live as they do. Great people such as Fan Jinshi protected our cultural relics so we can see them today. The Red Army's never-give-up spirit still gives us courage when we face hard work. Knowing history makes us wiser and more grateful.
passageZh:
学习历史对我们很重要。我们能了解过去的事物，如古代食物、古老建筑和重大事件，了解古人如何生活、国家如何发展。我们还能学习伟人精神，如保护历史的樊锦诗、有永不放弃精神的红军。历史给我们很多宝贵教训，帮助我们今天过上更好的生活。
历史就在我们身边，不只是课本里。镇上的老桥、祖父吃过的面条、我们仍庆祝的节日，都承载历史。学习过去帮助我们理解国家为何如此、人们为何这样生活。樊锦诗这样的伟人保护文物，让我们今天还能看到。红军永不放弃的精神仍在我们面对困难时给我们勇气。了解历史让我们更明智、更感恩。
source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U4测试卷笔试（基础卷·阅读选择）

title: Fan Jinshi protects Dunhuang
passage:
Fan Jinshi is a great woman who protects Dunhuang's art. When she first went to Dunhuang, life was difficult, and there were problems everywhere in the caves. But she loved the beautiful paintings on the walls. She and other people took photos of the paintings and used digital ways to show them. In this way, more people can enjoy the art, and the paintings in the caves are well protected. Fan Jinshi spent her life protecting Dunhuang's history, and we should learn from her.
Dunhuang lies in the Gobi Desert in northwest China. The Mogao Caves hold thousands of ancient wall paintings and sculptures made over a thousand years. When Fan Jinshi arrived in 1963, the caves were dusty and crumbling, and strong winds damaged the art every year. She spent her whole life living there, studying the paintings and raising money to protect them. Her team used digital cameras and computers to record the murals, so everyone in the world can see them online. People call her the Daughter of Dunhuang because she gave Dunhuang her youth and her heart.
passageZh:
樊锦诗是守护敦煌艺术的伟大女性。初到敦煌时生活艰难，洞窟里到处是问题，但她热爱墙上美丽的壁画。她和别人给壁画拍照，用数字方式展示，这样更多人能欣赏艺术，洞窟壁画也得到良好保护。樊锦诗一生守护敦煌历史，我们应向她学习。
敦煌位于中国西北戈壁。莫高窟藏有上千年来创作的数千幅古代壁画和雕塑。1963年樊锦诗初到时，洞窟积尘剥落，每年大风损害壁画。她一生住在那里，研究壁画、筹款保护。她的团队用数码相机和电脑记录壁画，让全世界都能在线看到。人们称她“敦煌女儿”，因为她把青春和心都给了敦煌。
source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U4测试卷笔试（基础卷·阅读判断改写）

title: The ancient dumpling on the Silk Road
passage:
Xinjiang was an important place on the ancient Silk Road. It was near the border between China and other countries, so people from East and West met there for trade. A long time ago, people from the Central Plains went to Xinjiang along the Silk Road and brought dumplings there. The ancient dumpling found in Xinjiang dates back to the Tang Dynasty. It's in the shape of a new moon and looks just like the dumplings we eat today.
The Silk Road was a long trade route linking China with Central Asia, West Asia and Europe. Along it, people carried silk, tea, spices and food between East and West. Xinjiang sat right in the middle of this road, so it became a busy meeting place for travellers and traders. The ancient dumpling found there shows that food also travelled along the road and took on local tastes. Today we can still taste that long history on our dinner table.

新疆是古丝绸之路上的重要地点，靠近中国与他国边境，东西方人在那里贸易。很久以前，中原人沿丝绸之路到新疆，把饺子带到那里。在新疆发现的古代饺子可追溯到唐朝，呈新月形，看起来和今天吃的饺子一模一样。
丝绸之路是连接中国与中亚、西亚、欧洲的漫长商路。人们沿路在东西方之间运输丝绸、茶叶、香料和食物。新疆正处在这条路中央，成为旅行者和商人繁忙的交汇地。在那里发现的古代饺子说明食物也沿路传播，并融入当地口味。今天我们仍能在餐桌上品尝那段悠久历史。

title: Mr Green's missing wallet
passage: Last Friday, Mr. Green couldn't find his wallet. He was very worried because there was some money and his ID card in it. He looked for it everywhere in his house—on the table, in the drawer, under the bed, but he didn't find it. Then his son Jack said, "Dad, let's think carefully. Where did you put it last time?" Mr. Green thought for a moment and said, "I put it in my coat pocket when I came back home yesterday evening." Jack checked the coat pocket and found the wallet there. Mr. Green was very thankful to Jack.

title: The missing necklace at the craft show
passage:
Last Friday, our school held a craft show. My friend Lucy lost her handmade necklace. It was made of colourful beads and was very special to her. She felt sad and asked me to be her detective partner.
First, we asked Lucy's deskmate, Lily. Lily said she didn't see the necklace. Then we thought: where did Lucy go before the show? She told us she went to the playground to get some fresh air. We went to the playground and looked carefully. Suddenly, I saw something shiny under a tree—it was Lucy's necklace! Lucy said she took it out of her bag to show a friend on the playground, and it must have fallen under the tree. Lucy was so happy to get it back. She said I was a clever detective because I used good thinking skills to find the clue.

passage: One night, a thief stole many jewels from a big house. The next morning, a detective came to look for clues. He walked around the house and looked carefully. title: Using leaves to find the way
passage: One day, a little boy was walking in the forest and lost his way. He took a deep breath and did not give up. He remembered his grandfather's words: use what is around you to help. He looked at the trees. On the side with more leaves, the sun shines more, so that side is south. He also used some long leaves to mark the path behind him. Slowly, he walked out of the forest and saw his village. His mother was worried, but she was so glad to see him. The boy learned that a calm mind and careful observation can work out any problem.

title: My school, then and now
passage:
My school has changed a lot. Ten years ago, it was small. There was only one tall building and a small playground. There were no computers in the classroom. Students had to read books to learn new things. The journey to school was hard for some students; they had to walk a long way.
Now my school is big and beautiful. There are three tall buildings and a big playground with a football field. Every classroom has many computers. Students can use the internet to learn more. All the students can take the school bus to school, so the journey is easy and safe. We all love our new school.

source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U6测试卷笔试（基础卷·阅读理解A篇）

title: Planting hope on the bare mountain
passage: Twenty years ago, the mountain near the village was bare. There were almost no trees, and the wind blew dust everywhere. Uncle Li and the villagers decided to change it. They started to plant trees on the mountain year after year. At first, many young trees died, but they did not give up. Today, there are millions of trees on the mountain. The weather is nice, and it is not windy and dusty any more. The mountain is green and the village is beautiful. When Uncle Li says "we planted hope", he means the mountain became green and the village got beautiful. Trees bring a better life to everyone.

source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U6测试卷图文（基础卷B篇）据参考解析整理

title: Mike's town, thirty years ago and now
passage:
Mike lives in a small town in the south of China. Thirty years ago, his town was very small. There were only a few small houses and narrow roads. There was no teahouse, no supermarket and no internet at home. People mainly travelled by bike or on foot.
Now the town is different. There are many tall buildings and shops. A beautiful teahouse stands by the river. Shared bikes are everywhere, and people can also travel by high-speed train. People have the internet at home and life is much easier. Mike says his town changes fast, but it keeps its warm heart.

source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U6测试卷图文（提高卷A篇）据参考解析整理

title: A village school, past and present
passage:
Ten years ago, the village school was small and old. There were only two small classrooms. The students had to climb wooden ladders to get to the small classroom on the second floor. There was no library and no digital TV in the classroom.
Now the school has changed. It has a small library with many books, and there is digital TV in every classroom. There is a big playground with a basketball court. Today, the students can learn more about the world through the internet and many books. They love their school.

title: Changes bring a better life
passage:
Thirty years ago, life in China was very different. People lived in small houses and there were not many cars. The streets were full of bikes, and most people went to work by bike. In the past, the journey to school was hard and dangerous; some children walked for hours over mountains.
Today, everything is different. There are lots of tall buildings and wide roads. People leave home in the morning and get to another city by high-speed train in hours. Grandpa told me some young people gave up a good life in the city to do something for their hometown. After 22 years, the Daliang Mountains became a green world with over 10 million trees. Changes bring us a better life, and we should love our country.
passageZh: 三十年前中国生活很不同。人们住小房子，汽车不多，街上满是自行车，多数人骑车上班。过去上学路艰难危险，有些孩子翻山走几小时。如今一切不同，有许多高楼宽路，人们早上离家，几小时坐高铁就到另一座城市。爷爷告诉我，有些年轻人放弃城里美好生活为家乡做事。22年后大凉山变成拥有上千万棵树的绿色世界。变化带来更好生活，我们应热爱祖国。
source: 外研版（2024新教材·三年级起点）；五下U6知识清单（Then and now）+联网复核原创

unit: Unit 1 What do you do with money?
title: The Golden Touch（教材Speed up）
passage:
Long long ago, there was a king called Midas. He loved gold very much. One day he met an old man. The old man said, "Do you have a wish? I can make it come true."
"I wish for a golden touch," said Midas. "I want to turn everything to gold!" "Are you sure?" "Yes. I am very sure."
Midas turned everything around him to gold. He was happy. Then Midas was hungry, but all his food also turned to gold. His daughter came in. Midas took her hand. She turned to gold, too! Midas was very sad. He cried, "I don't want gold now. I want food. I want my daughter back." He asked the old man to get everything back again. When he asked how much it would cost, the old man did not ask for gold; he only wanted Midas to learn the lesson. The old man smiled, "Just remember, gold isn't everything."
passageZh:
很久很久以前，有一位名叫迈达斯的国王，他非常热爱黄金。一天他遇见一位老人，老人说：“你有愿望吗？我能让它实现。”
“我希望有点石成金的本领，”迈达斯说，“我要把一切都变成黄金！”“你确定吗？”“是的，我非常确定。”
迈达斯把身边的一切都变成了黄金，他很开心。后来他饿了，可所有食物也变成了黄金。女儿走进来，迈达拉住她的手，她也变成了黄金！迈达斯非常伤心，哭着说：“我现在不要黄金了，我要食物，我要女儿回来。”他请老人把一切变回来。当他问要付出多少代价时，老人没有要黄金，只想让迈达斯吸取教训。老人笑着说：“记住，黄金不是万能的。”
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上教材PDF Speed up《The Golden Touch》（真实故事，Unit 1）

unit: Unit 1 What do you do with money?
title: Tom's Pocket Money
passage: Tom received fifty yuan every month as pocket money. At the shop, he always bought toys or sweets. He never saved a coin. One day, he saw a notice on the school board. It said that some children in the mountains had no new pencils or books. Tom felt a little sad, but he did not know what to do. His mother advised him to keep a money diary. She said, "Write down every yuan you spend. Then you will see where your money goes." Tom tried for one week. He found that he spent twenty yuan on crisps and chocolate. He was surprised. The next month, he decided to save half of his money. He put the coins in a piggy bank. After three months, he had seventy-five yuan. He sent the money to the children in the mountains with a short letter. A week later, he received a thank-you drawing from a girl there. Tom put the drawing on his wall. Now he still saves money, but he no longer buys unnecessary toys. He says, "Gold isn't everything, but a kind heart is." Sharing a small amount with people in need brings more joy than keeping it all.
passageZh: 汤姆每个月收到五十元零花钱。在商店里，他总是买玩具或糖果。他一个硬币也不存。一天，他在校报上看到一则通知。上面说，山区有些孩子没有新铅笔和新书。汤姆有点难过，但他不知道该怎么办。妈妈建议他记一本零花钱日记。她说：“把你花的每一元都记下来，这样你就会知道钱花到哪里去了。”汤姆试了一周。他发现自己在薯片和巧克力上花了二十元。他很惊讶。第二个月，他决定把一半的钱存起来。他把硬币放进存钱罐。三个月后，他有了七十五元。他把钱连同一封短信寄给了山区的孩子们。一周后，他收到那里一个女孩寄来的感谢画。汤姆把画贴在墙上。现在他仍然存钱，但不再买不必要的玩具。他说：“金子不是万能的，但一颗善良的心是。” 把一小部分分给需要帮助的人，比独自占有带来更多快乐。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 1语法与话题，非教材原文）

unit: Unit 1 What do you do with money?
title: Two Boys and a Golden Egg
passage: Once there were two brothers, Sam and Tim. They found a wooden box under an old tree. Inside, there was a shiny golden egg. Sam shouted, "We are rich! Let's sell it and buy a big house." Tim was quiet. He said, "Wait. Whose box is this? We should ask around." Sam did not listen. He ran to the market and tried to sell the egg. A wise old man looked at it and smiled. He said, "This is not real gold. It is a painted stone. It looks valuable, but it is worth nothing." Sam's face turned red. He went home and felt ashamed. Tim was not angry. He said, "Don't worry. Remember, gold isn't everything. Let's use our hands to make real money." The two brothers started a small garden. They grew vegetables and sold them every weekend. Slowly, they earned their own money. They learned that true value does not come from a lucky find, but from hard work and honesty.
passageZh: 从前有兄弟俩，萨姆和蒂姆。他们在一棵老树下发现了一个木盒子。里面有一枚闪亮的金蛋。萨姆大叫：“我们发财了！把它卖了，买栋大房子。”蒂姆很安静。他说：“等等。这盒子是谁的？我们应该问问。”萨姆不听。他跑到集市上，想把金蛋卖掉。一位聪明的老人看了看，笑了。他说：“这不是真金子，只是一块上了漆的石头。它看起来值钱，其实一文不值。”萨姆的脸涨得通红。他回到家，感到羞愧。蒂姆并没有生气。他说：“别担心。记住，金子不是万能的。我们用双手去赚真正的钱吧。”兄弟俩开了一个小菜园。他们种蔬菜，每个周末拿去卖。慢慢地，他们赚到了自己的钱。他们明白了，真正的价值不来自幸运的捡到，而来自努力和诚实。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 1语法与话题，非教材原文）

unit: Unit 1 What do you do with money?
title: Buying a Birthday Gift
passage: It was Grandma's seventieth birthday, and Lisa wanted to buy a special gift. She had saved forty yuan in her drawer. On Saturday, she went to the market with her mother. First, she saw a beautiful hat. "How much is it?" she asked. The seller said thirty-five yuan. Lisa tried it on, but Grandma already had three hats. Then she saw a box of tea. It was twenty-eight yuan, but Grandma did not drink tea. Next, she saw a young girl selling hand-made cloth bags. The bags were colourful and strong. Lisa picked a blue one with a small rabbit on it. "How much is this bag?" she asked. The girl said fifteen yuan. Lisa thought, "Grandma carries many things when she goes shopping. This bag is just right." She paid and took the bag home. On the birthday, she gave it to Grandma. Grandma held it and said, "This is the best gift, because you chose it with your heart." Lisa learned that an expensive gift is not always the best. The thought behind it matters most.
passageZh: 奶奶要过七十岁生日了，丽莎想买一份特别的礼物。她抽屉里攒了四十元。周六，她和妈妈去了集市。首先，她看到一顶漂亮的帽子。“这个多少钱？”她问。摊主说三十五元。丽莎试戴了一下，可奶奶已经有三顶帽子了。然后她看到一盒茶叶。二十八元，但奶奶不喝茶。接着，她看到一个小女孩在卖手工布包。这些包色彩鲜艳，又结实。丽莎挑了一个蓝色的，上面有一只小兔子。“这个包多少钱？”她问。女孩说十五元。丽莎想：“奶奶买菜时要带很多东西。这个包正合适。”她付了钱，把包带回家。生日那天，她把包送给奶奶。奶奶捧着包说：“这是最好的礼物，因为你是用心挑的。”丽莎明白了，贵的礼物不一定最好。礼物背后的心意才最重要。

unit: Unit 1 What do you do with money?
title: The Box for the Poor
passage: Mr Brown was a kind shopkeeper. At the door of his fruit shop, he placed a big brown box. On the box, there was a sign: "Take what you need. Pay what you can." Inside, he put fresh apples, oranges and bread. Poor people could take food without paying. Some kind customers also put food into the box. At first, some people laughed at Mr Brown. They said he would lose all his money. But months passed, and his shop became busier than before. People came from far away to buy fruit from the kind shopkeeper. One cold evening, a hungry old man took an apple from the box. He had no money at all. Mr Brown smiled and gave him a hot cup of tea. The old man said, "You give so much. How can you afford it?" Mr Brown answered, "I don't give because I am rich. I give because I know how it feels to be hungry. When we help others, we build a warmer neighbourhood." That night, Mr Brown found a small envelope in the box. Inside was fifty yuan and a note: "Thank you. I am fine now."
passageZh: 布朗先生是一位善良的店主。在他水果店门口，放着一个棕色的大箱子。箱子上有一块牌子：“需要就拿，能付就付。”里面放着新鲜的苹果、橙子和面包。穷人可以不付钱就拿走食物。一些好心的顾客也会把食物放进箱子。起初，有些人嘲笑布朗先生。他们说他会把钱全赔光。但几个月过去了，他的店比以前更热闹了。人们从远处赶来，向这位善良的店主买水果。一个寒冷的傍晚，一位饥饿的老人从箱子里拿了一个苹果。他身上一分钱也没有。布朗先生笑了，还给他一杯热茶。老人说：“你付出这么多，怎么负担得起？”布朗先生回答：“我给予，不是因为我富有。我给予，是因为我懂得饥饿的滋味。当我们帮助别人，我们就建成了一个更温暖的社区。”那天晚上，布朗先生在箱子里发现了一个小信封。里面有五十元和一张纸条：“谢谢你。我现在好了。”
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 1语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: Crayons' Letters（教材Speed up）
passage:
Duncan opens his box of colours. His crayons are still in the box, but they have left him letters.
Grey: You use me to colour big animals. I'm now shorter than my friends! I want to colour smaller things.
Pink: Remember me? It's Pink and I'm angry. You never use me. Why? Boys can use the colour pink! A pink dinosaur is good, too.
Black: It's Black, and I'm unhappy. You only use me for lines. How about a black rainbow next time?
White: I'm sad. You always use white paper and no one can see me.
At last, Duncan listens to them, and draws a picture they all like, using every colour. Even the smallest crayon has its own place in the picture.
passageZh:
邓肯打开彩笔盒，蜡笔还在里面，却给他留下了一封封信。
灰色：你总用我画大动物，我现在比朋友们都短了！我想画小一点的东西。
粉色：还记得我吗？我是粉色，我很生气。你从不使用我，男孩也能用粉色，一只粉色恐龙也很棒。
黑色：我是黑色，我不开心。你只用我画线条，下次来条黑色彩虹怎么样？
白色：我很难过，你总用白纸，没人看得见我。
最后，邓肯听了它们的话，用上每种颜色，画了一幅大家都喜欢的画，就连最小的蜡笔也在画里有自己的位置。

title: Fruit or Juice?
passage: Many children think that fruit juice is as healthy as fresh fruit. Is that true? Dr Lee gave a talk at our school last week. She said that a whole apple is better than a glass of apple juice. When you eat an apple, you get the fibre, which helps your body. But when fruit is made into juice, the fibre is often lost. Also, most juice drinks have a lot of added sugar. A bottle of juice may contain more sugar than a bar of chocolate. Dr Lee showed us two pictures. One showed a fresh apple, and the other showed five apples squeezed into one small cup of juice. She said, "Why not just eat the apple? It is simpler and healthier." Some students were surprised. Tom used to drink two bottles of juice every day. He decided to change. Now he eats one apple and drinks a glass of water after lunch. He says he feels less thirsty and more active. Dr Lee also told us the old saying: "An apple a day keeps the doctor away."
passageZh: 很多孩子认为果汁和新鲜水果一样健康。是这样吗？上周李医生在我校做了一次讲座。她说，一个完整的苹果比一杯苹果汁更好。吃苹果时，你摄入了帮助身体的纤维。但水果榨成汁后，纤维往往就流失了。而且，大多数果汁饮料加了很多糖。一瓶果汁所含的糖，可能比一块巧克力还多。李医生给我们看了两张图。一张是一个新鲜苹果，另一张是五个苹果榨成的一小杯果汁。她说：“为什么不直接吃苹果呢？更简单，也更健康。”一些学生很惊讶。汤姆以前每天喝两瓶果汁。他决定改变。现在他午饭后吃一个苹果，喝一杯水。他说自己不那么渴了，也更有活力。李医生还告诉我们那句老话：“一天一苹果，医生远离我。”
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 2语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: Lily's Opinion About Breakfast
passage: In my opinion, breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Some of my classmates skip breakfast because they get up late. They say they are not hungry in the morning. But I don't think so. I feel tired if I do not eat breakfast, and I cannot listen carefully in class. Last week, our science teacher did a small test. We compared two groups. Group One ate eggs, bread and milk for breakfast. Group Two ate only a sweet cake. After two hours, Group One was much more active. The children who ate sweet food became sleepy very early. Our teacher explained: sweet food gives a quick but short energy, while milk and eggs give a longer and steadier energy. In my opinion, a good breakfast should include milk, eggs or bread, and some fruit. It is better to get up ten minutes earlier than to skip breakfast. I hope everyone in my class will start the day with a good breakfast. An apple a day keeps the doctor away, but a good breakfast keeps the sleepyhead away!
passageZh: 在我看来，早餐是一天中最重要的一餐。我的一些同学因为起得晚而不吃早餐。他们说早上不饿。但我不这么认为。如果不吃早餐，我会觉得累，上课也听不进去。上周，我们科学老师做了一个小测试。我们比较了两组。第一组早餐吃鸡蛋、面包和牛奶。第二组只吃一块甜蛋糕。两小时后，第一组活跃得多。吃甜食的孩子很早就犯困。老师解释说：甜食提供快速但短暂的能量，而牛奶和鸡蛋提供更持久、更稳定的能量。在我看来，一顿好早餐应该包括牛奶、鸡蛋或面包，再加一些水果。早起十分钟，也比不吃早餐好。我希望班上每个人都能以一顿好早餐开始新的一天。一天一苹果，医生远离我；而一顿好早餐，赶走瞌睡虫！
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 2语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: Food Around the World
passage: People in different countries eat different food, but healthy eating is the same everywhere. In China, people eat rice, vegetables and fish. In Japan, people often eat fish and rice, and they are one of the healthiest nations in the world. In Italy, people eat bread, tomatoes and olive oil. In India, many people eat lentils, rice and spicy vegetables. Although the food is different, experts agree on a few rules. First, eat more vegetables and fruit than meat. Second, do not eat too much fried food. Third, drink water instead of sweet drinks. A study shows that countries with simple, natural food have fewer heart problems. Fast food is popular because it is fast and cheap. But it is usually saltier and oilier than home cooking. In my opinion, we can enjoy fast food sometimes, but not every day. As the saying goes, "You are what you eat." If we choose fresh and balanced food, our body will thank us.
passageZh: 不同国家的人吃不同的食物，但健康饮食在世界各地都是一样的。在中国，人们吃米饭、蔬菜和鱼。在日本，人们常吃鱼和米饭，他们是世界上最健康的民族之一。在意大利，人们吃面包、西红柿和橄榄油。在印度，很多人吃小扁豆、米饭和辣味蔬菜。虽然食物不同，但专家们在几条规则上达成一致。第一，蔬菜和水果要比肉吃得多。第二，不要吃太多油炸食品。第三，喝水而不是甜饮料。一项研究表明，食用简单天然食物的国家，心脏问题更少。快餐很受欢迎，因为它又快又便宜。但它通常比家常菜更咸、更油。在我看来，我们可以偶尔吃快餐，但不能每天吃。正如谚语所说：“人如其食。”如果我们选择新鲜、均衡的食物，身体会感谢我们。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 2语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: A Family Cooking Day
passage: Last Sunday, the Greens had a Family Cooking Day. Mum put on a colourful apron, and Dad washed the vegetables. The children, Lily and Jack, decided to make a healthy lunch together. They made tomato and egg soup, steamed fish, green beans and a fruit salad. Lily wanted to put lots of sugar in the salad, but Mum said, "Fruit is already sweet. Sugar is less healthy than natural taste." Jack agreed. He said, "An apple a day keeps the doctor away, so let's put apples in the salad." Dad cut the fish carefully. He said boiled fish was healthier than fried fish. The kitchen was busy and noisy, but everyone had fun. At noon, they sat around the table. The food was simple, but it tasted better than any restaurant meal. Lily said that home cooking was warmer and healthier than fast food. Jack asked if they could have a Cooking Day every month. Mum smiled and said yes. The family learned that cooking together was not only about food, but also about love.
passageZh: 上周日，格林家举办了“家庭烹饪日”。妈妈系上彩色围裙，爸爸洗蔬菜。孩子们莉莉和杰克决定一起做一顿健康午餐。他们做了西红柿鸡蛋汤、清蒸鱼、青豆和一份水果沙拉。莉莉想在沙拉里放很多糖，但妈妈说：“水果本来就是甜的。糖不如天然的味道健康。”杰克同意。他说：“一天一苹果，医生远离我，那我们把苹果放进沙拉吧。”爸爸小心地切鱼。他说水煮鱼比炸鱼更健康。厨房又忙又闹，但大家都很开心。中午，他们围坐在桌旁。食物简单，却比任何餐馆的饭都好吃。莉莉说，家常菜比快餐更温暖、更健康。杰克问能不能每个月都办一次烹饪日。妈妈笑着答应了。这家人明白了，一起下厨不仅是为了食物，更是为了爱。

title: Xu Xiake, the Great Traveller（教材Speed up）
passage:
Xu Xiake is one of the most famous travellers in China. He was interested in nature from a young age. He read many books about famous mountains and rivers. He wanted to see them with his own eyes.
Xu Xiake started to travel at the age of 21. He visited many places in China. He wrote about mountains and rivers, like Mount Huangshan and the Jinsha River. From his words, people today learn about the China of his days.
Xu Xiake loved nature. Some people did bad things to it. He was angry and always called for people to take care of nature. He travelled for about 30 years. He said, "I went to so many wonderful places in China. I had a wonderful life." His words later became a famous book that travellers still read with great interest today.
passageZh:
徐霞客是中国最著名的旅行家之一。他从小对大自然感兴趣，读了许多名山大川的书，想亲眼去看看。
徐霞客21岁开始游历，走遍中国许多地方，写下关于黄山、金沙江等山川河流的文字。今天的人们通过他的文字了解他那个时代的中国。
徐霞客热爱自然，看到有人破坏自然时他很愤怒，总是呼吁人们爱护自然。他游历了约30年，说：“我走遍了中国这么多美好的地方，我的一生很精彩。”他写下的文字后来成为一本名著，今天的旅行者仍饶有兴致地阅读。

title: Xu Xiake, the Great Traveller
passage: Xu Xiake is one of the most famous travellers in Chinese history. He was born in 1587, in the Ming Dynasty. When he was a boy, he loved reading books about mountains and rivers. His dream was to see them with his own eyes. At that time, most people stayed close to home. But Xu Xiake wanted to explore the world. For more than thirty years, he travelled on foot and on horseback. He climbed dangerous mountains, crossed deep rivers and walked through thick forests. He did not travel for fun only. Every day, he wrote in his diary. He described rocks, rivers, plants and the homes of local people. His notes later became a great book called The Travel Diaries of Xu Xiake. Modern scientists are surprised by his records. They say his descriptions of caves and rivers are surprisingly accurate. Xu Xiake did not have a plane or a camera, but his love for nature made him a true explorer. His story tells us that if you keep a curious heart, the whole world becomes a book.
passageZh: 徐霞客是中国历史上最著名的旅行家之一。他生于1587年，明朝。小时候，他就喜欢读关于山川河流的书。他的梦想是亲眼看看它们。那时，大多数人都守在家门口。但徐霞客想探索世界。三十多年里，他步行、骑马游历四方。他攀登险峻的高山，渡过深河，穿越茂密的森林。他旅行不只是为了好玩。他每天都写日记。他描述岩石、河流、植物和当地人的生活。他的记录后来汇成了一部伟大的书——《徐霞客游记》。现代科学家对他的记录感到惊讶。他们说他对洞穴和河流的描述惊人地准确。徐霞客没有飞机，也没有相机，但对自然的热爱使他成为一位真正的探险家。他的故事告诉我们，只要保持一颗好奇的心，整个世界都会成为一本书。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 3语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: A Trip to the National Park
passage: Last summer, our class went to Zhangjiajie National Park. We went there by bus early in the morning. When we arrived, we saw tall, strange mountains rising straight into the clouds. Our teacher said these mountains were made of stone, and the wind and rain had shaped them over millions of years. We took a small train through a deep valley. The trees were so thick that the sun could hardly reach the ground. We saw colourful birds and heard monkeys jumping in the trees. At noon, we had a picnic near a clear river. The water was so cold that our fingers turned red. In the afternoon, we walked along a glass bridge high above the valley. Some of us were afraid to look down, but the view was amazing. Our teacher told us not to drop litter. She said, "These rocks and trees have lived for millions of years. We are only visitors. We must leave them as we found them." On the way home, everyone was tired, but no one stopped talking about the trip. We all agreed that protecting nature is everyone's duty.
passageZh: 去年夏天，我们班去了张家界国家公园。我们一大早就坐大巴出发。到达时，我们看到一座座又高又奇的山峰直插云端。老师说，这些山是石头构成的，风雨经过数百万年把它们雕琢成这样。我们乘小火车穿过一个幽深的山谷。树木茂密，阳光几乎照不到地面。我们看到了色彩鲜艳的鸟，听到猴子在树上跳跃。中午，我们在一条清澈的小河边野餐。水冰凉，我们的手指都冻红了。下午，我们走过一座高悬于山谷之上的玻璃桥。我们中有些人不敢往下看，但景色令人惊叹。老师叫我们不要乱扔垃圾。她说：“这些岩石和树木已经存在了数百万年。我们只是访客。我们必须让它们保持原样。”回家的路上，大家都很累，但没人停止谈论这次旅行。我们都认为，保护自然是每个人的责任。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 3语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: The Amazon Rainforest
passage: The Amazon rainforest is the largest forest on the earth. It covers most of Brazil and eight other countries. People call it the "lungs of the earth", because it produces a huge amount of oxygen. Millions of kinds of animals and plants live there. Some of them have not even been discovered by scientists. The forest is always wet and warm. Tall trees block the sunlight, so the ground below is dark and quiet. However, this amazing forest is getting smaller every year. People cut down trees to make farms, roads and shopping centres. When the trees disappear, many animals lose their homes. The climate also changes, because the forest can no longer hold so much water. Experts say that if we lose the Amazon, the whole planet will feel the effect. Some groups are working hard to stop the cutting. They plant new trees and teach local people how to live without destroying the forest. In my opinion, protecting the rainforest is not just one country's business. It is a duty for everyone on the earth. The next generation should be able to walk into a living forest, not a dead one.
passageZh: 亚马孙雨林是地球上最大的森林。它覆盖了巴西大部分地区和另外八个国家。人们称它为“地球之肺”，因为它产生大量氧气。数百万种动植物生活在那里。其中有些甚至还没有被科学家发现。森林总是又湿又暖。高大的树木遮住阳光，所以下面的地面又黑又安静。然而，这片神奇的森林每年都在变小。人们砍伐树木来建农场、修道路、盖购物中心。树木消失时，许多动物失去了家园。气候也随之改变，因为森林再也无法蓄存这么多水。专家说，如果失去亚马孙，整个地球都会受到影响。一些团体正在努力制止砍伐。他们种植新树，并教当地人如何在不破坏森林的情况下生活。在我看来，保护雨林不只是一个国家的事。它是地球上每个人的责任。下一代应该能够走进一片活着的森林，而不是死去的森林。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 3语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: The Longest River Quiz
passage: Last Monday, our teacher held a "Wonders of Nature" quiz. There were five groups, and our group hoped to win. The first question was: "What is the longest river in the world?" Daming quickly said, "The Nile!" The teacher nodded and gave us ten points. The next question was: "Which is the highest mountain?" We answered Mount Qomolangma. Then came a hard one: "Which is the deepest lake in the world?" We thought for a minute. Lingling said, "Baikal!" It was correct. The last question was a surprise: "Who wrote about Chinese mountains and rivers more than three hundred years ago?" We looked at each other. Suddenly, Sam shouted, "Xu Xiake!" We won the quiz by two points. After that, the teacher showed us photos of different wonders. She said, "There are so many wonders on the earth, but we must protect them." We decided to make a poster about nature protection for our school. The quiz was not only about remembering facts. It made us love and care for our beautiful planet.
passageZh: 上周一，老师举办了一场“自然奇观”知识竞赛。全班分五个组，我们组希望能赢。第一个问题是：“世界上最长的河是哪条？”大明马上说：“尼罗河！”老师点点头，给了我们十分。下一个问题是：“哪座山最高？”我们回答珠穆朗玛峰。接着来了个难题：“世界上最深的湖是哪个？”我们想了一会儿。玲玲说：“贝加尔湖！”答对了。最后一个问题出人意料：“三百多年前，是谁写下了关于中国山川河流的文字？”我们面面相觑。突然，萨姆喊道：“徐霞客！”我们以两分的优势赢得了比赛。之后，老师给我们看了不同奇观的照片。她说：“地球上有这么多奇观，但我们必须保护它们。”我们决定为学校制作一张关于自然保护的海报。这场竞赛不只是记忆事实。它让我们热爱并关心我们美丽的星球。

title: Lu Ban and the Umbrella（教材Speed up）
passage:
It was raining. Grandpa gave Lingling an umbrella. "Grandpa, who first got the idea of making an umbrella?" she asked.
Grandpa said no one knows for sure, but stories say it was Lu Ban. One day, Lu Ban was on the way home and it rained. He thought, "What can I make to keep off the rain?" Just then, he saw a boy with a big leaf over his head. "That's a good idea!" Lu Ban said.
First, he used bamboo to make the sticks. Next, he cut some cloth. Then, he put the cloth over the sticks. That was the first umbrella! Lu Ban had great ideas and clever hands. People still tell his story today because it reminds us that a useful idea can come from anything we notice around us.
passageZh:
天在下雨，爷爷递给玲玲一把伞。“爷爷，是谁最先想出做伞的主意？”她问。
爷爷说没人说得准，传说说是鲁班。一天鲁班回家路上，下起雨。他想：“我能做什么来挡雨？”就在这时，他看见一个男孩头顶一片大叶子。“好主意！”鲁班说。
首先，他用竹子做伞骨。接着，他剪下一块布。然后，把布盖在伞骨上。这就是第一把伞！鲁班既有好点子，又有巧手。人们至今还讲他的故事，因为它提醒我们，有用的主意可以来自身边任何被留意到的事物。

title: The Recycling Club
passage: Our school started a Recycling Club this term. Every Wednesday afternoon, members meet in the art room. We collect clean waste from each classroom: old paper, plastic bottles, cans and pieces of cloth. Then we turn them into new things. Last month, we made shopping bags from old T-shirts. We cut the sleeves off and tied the bottom. The bags were strong enough to carry books. We also made pencil holders from tall cans. We covered the cans with colourful paper and stuck buttons on them. The best project was the bird house. We used old wood and empty milk cartons. We hung the bird houses in the school garden, and soon some sparrows moved in. Our teacher said recycling saves energy. Making a new bottle uses much more energy than reusing an old one. She also said every small action counts. Now the Recycling Club has more than forty members. We plan to make flower pots from old newspapers for the coming spring. We invite everyone to join us and make the earth a cleaner place.

title: A Dress from an Old Scarf
passage: Last winter, Anna's mother gave her a beautiful dress. It was not new from a shop. Her mother made it from an old wool scarf. The scarf was Anna's grandmother's. It had a small hole on one corner, so no one wore it. Anna's mother did not throw it away. She washed it, cut the hole off, and sewed it into a warm little dress. The dress was soft and blue, with two buttons on the front. Anna loved it very much. At school, her friend Julia asked where she bought it. Anna smiled and said, "My mum made it from Grandma's old scarf." Julia was surprised. She said, "I have an old sweater at home with a hole. Can your mum help me?" Anna's mother agreed. Soon, she helped several girls turn old clothes into new bags and scarves. The children learnt that old cloth does not have to be rubbish. It can become something full of love. This spring, Anna wore her blue dress to a school show. She felt proud, because her dress carried Grandma's memory and Mum's care.
passageZh: 去年冬天，安娜的妈妈送了她一条漂亮的连衣裙。它不是从商店买的新衣服。她妈妈用一条旧羊毛围巾改成的。这条围巾是安娜奶奶的。它一角有个小洞，所以没人戴了。安娜的妈妈没有把它扔掉。她把它洗净，剪掉破洞，缝成一条暖和的小裙子。裙子是柔软的蓝色，前面有两颗纽扣。安娜非常喜欢。在学校，她的朋友朱莉娅问她在哪里买的。安娜笑着说：“我妈妈用奶奶的旧围巾做的。”朱莉娅很惊讶。她说：“我家有一件破洞的旧毛衣。你妈妈能帮帮我吗？”安娜的妈妈答应了。很快，她帮几个女孩把旧衣服改成新包和新围巾。孩子们懂得了，旧布料不一定要成为垃圾。它可以变成充满爱的东西。今年春天，安娜穿着蓝裙子参加学校演出。她感到自豪，因为她的裙子带着奶奶的回忆和妈妈的爱。

title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
passage: You may have heard the three words: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. They are the rules for a greener life. "Reduce" means use less. For example, take your own bag to the shop, so you do not need a new plastic one. Turn off the light when you leave a room. "Reuse" means use things again. Don't throw away a glass jar. You can keep pencils or sweets in it. Give old books to a library instead of putting them in the bin. "Recycle" means change waste into new materials. Paper, glass, cans and plastic can be processed and made into new products. Many families in our street now sort their rubbish into four boxes: paper, plastic, glass and kitchen waste. Kitchen waste can become natural fertilizer for plants. Our class did a survey. We found that each student threw away about three plastic bottles a week. That is over one hundred bottles a year, for one child alone. If everyone reduces a little, the numbers will drop. We do not need great heroes. We need millions of people who do small things right.
passageZh: 你可能听过这三个词：减少、重复使用、回收利用。它们是更绿色生活的准则。“减少”意味着少用。比如，自带袋子去商店，这样就不需要新的塑料袋。离开房间时关灯。“重复使用”意味着再用一次。不要把玻璃罐扔掉。你可以用它装铅笔或糖果。把旧书捐给图书馆，而不是丢进垃圾桶。“回收利用”意味着把废物变成新材料。纸、玻璃、金属罐和塑料可以被加工成新产品。我们街上很多家庭现在把垃圾分类放进四个箱子：纸、塑料、玻璃和厨余。厨余可以变成植物的天然肥料。我们班做了一次调查。我们发现每个学生每周大约扔掉三个塑料瓶。对一个孩子来说，一年就是一百多个瓶子。如果每个人都少用一点，数字就会下降。我们不需要伟大的英雄。我们需要千百万把小事做对的人。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 4语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: The Old Box of Buttons
passage: When Mrs Lee was young, she lived with her grandmother. Her grandmother had a wooden box under the bed. It was full of buttons of all colours and sizes. When a coat was torn, she did not throw it away. She cut off the buttons and kept them in the box. Years later, the buttons became useful again. When a child lost a button on a school uniform, grandmother would find a matching one from her box. When a curtain was torn, she used buttons to make a new design. Mrs Lee remembered this when she became a mother. She started her own button box. Now her daughter, Xiao Yu, is using it too. Last week, Xiao Yu made a beautiful picture by gluing colourful buttons onto a piece of cardboard. It became the best art work in her class. The family also uses old bottles as vases and old T-shirts as cleaning cloths. They never feel poor, because they have imagination. Waste is just something waiting for a new idea.
passageZh: 李太太年轻时和奶奶住在一起。她奶奶床下有一个木盒子。里面装满了各种颜色、各种大小的纽扣。衣服破了，她不会扔掉。她把纽扣剪下来，收进盒子。多年以后，这些纽扣又派上了用场。当孩子校服上掉了一颗纽扣，奶奶会从盒子里找一颗相配的。窗帘破了，她用纽扣做出新的花样。李太太当妈妈后记住了这一点。她开始了自己的纽扣盒。现在她的女儿小雨也在用。上周，小雨把彩色纽扣粘在硬纸板上，做成了一幅美丽的画。它成了班上最好的美术作品。这家人还用旧瓶子当花瓶，用旧T恤当抹布。他们从不觉得穷，因为他们有想象力。废物，不过是在等待一个新点子。

title: Mary's Eyes（教材Speed up）
passage:
Mary could not see well. Yesterday, Miss Green wrote a "3" on the blackboard, but Mary saw an "8"! Mum took her to the doctor.
Doctor: Mary, do you often read in dark places? Mary: Yes, I like reading in bed at night. Doctor: And do you watch a lot of TV?
Mary nodded again. She also sat close to the screen and forgot to rest her eyes between long sessions.
Something is wrong with Mary's eyes, but it's not a big problem. They can get better. Doctor: Do eye exercises every day. Don't read in the dark. Go out often and look far away. You should take care of your eyes. After the visit, Mary promised to change her habits and let her eyes rest for a while every day.

医生：玛丽，你常在暗处看书吗？玛丽：是的，我喜欢晚上躺在床上看书。医生：那你是不是还看很多电视？
玛丽的眼睛有点问题，但不是大毛病，可以好转。医生：每天做眼保健操，别在暗处看书，常到户外远眺。你应该爱护自己的眼睛。看完医生后，玛丽答应改变习惯，每天让眼睛休息一会儿。

title: Ten Rules for a Healthy Life
passage: Do you want to be healthy and strong? Here are ten simple rules from a school doctor. First, drink enough water every day, about six glasses. Second, sleep for at least eight hours. Children who sleep less often feel tired in class. Third, eat more vegetables and fruit, and fewer sweets. Fourth, do sports for at least one hour a day. You can run, swim, ride a bike or play basketball. Fifth, do not read in the sun or in the dark, because your eyes are precious. Sixth, wash your hands before meals and after playing outside, because clean hands keep germs away. Seventh, when you are ill, take medicine on time and rest. Do not go to school with a high fever. Eighth, keep a smile on your face. Scientists say happy people are often healthier. Ninth, be kind to others. Helping friends brings you happiness, and happiness is good for your body. Tenth, remember that health is more important than marks or games. If you follow these rules, you will grow up strong. Just put a smile on your face and gladly face your day!
passageZh: 你想健康又强壮吗？下面是一位校医给出的十条简单规则。第一，每天喝足够的水，大约六杯。第二，至少睡八小时。睡眠不足的孩子上课常常觉得累。第三，多吃蔬菜和水果，少吃甜食。第四，每天至少运动一小时。你可以跑步、游泳、骑车或打篮球。第五，不要在阳光下或黑暗中看书，因为你的眼睛很珍贵。第六，饭前和在外面玩过之后要洗手，因为干净的手能挡住病菌。第七，生病时按时吃药并休息。发高烧不要去上学。第八，脸上常带微笑。科学家说，快乐的人往往更健康。第九，善待他人。帮助朋友会给你带来快乐，而快乐对身体有益。第十，记住，健康比分数或游戏更重要。如果你遵守这些规则，你会长得强壮。面带微笑，开心地面对每一天吧！
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 5语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: The Boy Who Hated Carrots
passage: Peter was a strong boy, but he had one problem: he hated vegetables. Every dinner, he pushed the carrots and beans to the side of his plate. His mother tried everything. She boiled them, fried them, and even hid them in soup. Peter still found them and left them. One day, Peter felt very tired in PE class. He could not run as fast as the other boys. The teacher asked him to see the school doctor. The doctor checked Peter and said, "Your body is running out of vitamins. You eat too much meat and chips, but too few vegetables." Peter was surprised. The doctor gave him a small task. For two weeks, Peter had to try one new vegetable every day. He did not have to love it; he just had to taste it. On the first day, he tried a small piece of carrot. It was sweeter than he thought. On the third day, he liked the beans. By the end of the two weeks, Peter asked his mother to cook vegetables again. He could run faster now. Peter learned that healthy food is not the enemy. It gives us the energy to play, study and grow.
passageZh: 彼得是个强壮的男孩，但他有一个问题：他讨厌蔬菜。每次晚饭，他都把胡萝卜和豆子拨到盘子边上。他妈妈试了各种办法。她煮、炸，甚至把它们藏进汤里。彼得还是把它们找出来剩下。一天，彼得在体育课上觉得很累。他跑不过其他男孩。老师让他去看校医。医生给彼得做了检查，说：“你的身体缺乏维生素。你肉和薯条吃得太多，蔬菜吃得太少。”彼得很惊讶。医生给了他一个小任务。两周里，彼得每天必须尝一种新蔬菜。他不必爱上它，只需尝一口。第一天，他尝了一小片胡萝卜。它比他想象的甜。第三天，他喜欢上了豆子。两周结束时，彼得主动让妈妈再做蔬菜。他现在能跑得更快了。彼得明白了，健康食物不是敌人。它给我们玩耍、学习和成长的能量。

title: Mental Health Matters Too
passage: When we talk about health, we often think of bodies. But a healthy mind is just as important. Lately, Jack had been quiet and sad. He did not want to play football with his friends, and he even forgot his homework. His mother was worried. She sat with him and asked, "Is anything making you unhappy?" Jack said, "I am afraid of the English test. I think I will fail, and everyone will laugh at me." His mother hugged him. She said, "It is OK to fail. Many clever people failed many times before they succeeded." She told him to talk to his teacher. The teacher was kind. She helped Jack make a study plan, and they practised together after class. Slowly, Jack became braver. He did not get a full mark in the end, but he passed. More importantly, he felt happy again. The school doctor says that when you feel sad, you should not keep it inside. You can talk to your parents, your teacher or a trusted friend. Be kind to others, and it will bring you happiness. A smile on the face is like a bandage for a tired heart.
passageZh: 当我们谈论健康时，常常想到身体。但健康的心灵同样重要。最近，杰克一直沉默又难过。他不想和朋友踢足球，甚至忘记作业。他妈妈很担心。她和他坐下来，问：“有什么让你不开心的事吗？”杰克说：“我害怕英语考试。我觉得我会不及格，大家会笑话我。”妈妈抱住他。她说：“失败没关系。很多聪明的人在成功之前也失败过很多次。”她让他去和老师谈谈。老师很和蔼。她帮杰克制定学习计划，课后一起练习。慢慢地，杰克变得勇敢了。最后他虽然没有得满分，但及格了。更重要的是，他又快乐起来。校医说，当你难过时，不要把情绪藏在心里。你可以告诉父母、老师或信任的朋友。善待他人，这会给你带来快乐。脸上的一个微笑，就像给疲惫心灵的创可贴。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 5语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: A Good Night's Sleep
passage: Sleep is like a silent doctor. While we sleep, our body repairs itself. Our brain organises what we learned during the day. However, many children do not sleep enough. A survey in our city showed that about sixty percent of Grade Six students slept less than eight hours. The main reason was screens. Many children played on their phones or watched videos until after ten o'clock. A doctor said that too much screen light makes the brain think it is still daytime. As a result, children feel tired the next day. They cannot listen carefully, and they may even feel ill. The doctor gave some advice. First, stop using screens one hour before bed. Second, keep the bedroom dark and quiet. Third, go to bed at the same time every night. Fourth, do not drink sweet drinks in the evening. After reading the survey, our class made a "Sleep Pact". We agreed to turn off our phones at nine thirty. After two weeks, most of us said we felt more awake in class. A good night's sleep costs nothing, but it gives us everything.
passageZh: 睡眠就像一位无声的医生。我们睡觉时，身体在自我修复。大脑整理白天学到的东西。然而，很多孩子睡眠不足。我们城市的一项调查显示，大约百分之六十的六年级学生睡眠少于八小时。主要原因是屏幕。很多孩子玩手机或看视频直到十点以后。医生说，过多的屏幕光线会让大脑以为还是白天。结果，孩子们第二天觉得累。他们无法专心听讲，甚至可能生病。医生给了一些建议。第一，睡前一小时停止使用屏幕。第二，保持卧室黑暗安静。第三，每天晚上同一时间上床。第四，晚上不要喝甜饮料。读完调查后，我们班制定了一份“睡眠公约”。我们同意九点半关掉手机。两周后，大多数人说自己上课更有精神了。一夜好眠分文不花，却给了我们一切。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 5语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: A Traveller's Diary in China（教材Speed up）
passage:
Sunday, 19 March: I'm now in China. I will ride around the country. China is so big, but it is a beautiful and interesting place. I just want to see it with my own eyes.
Sunday, 26 March: It's very hot today. I lost my water bottle. I went to a house by the road for help. I can't speak any Chinese, but they got it! They gave me some water and asked me to stay for lunch. How lucky I am!
Thursday, 13 April: I'm in Yunnan now. It's the Water-splashing Festival! People celebrate the Dai New Year. They splash water on each other. To them, this will bring good luck to others. How lucky I am to be here! I will always remember the kind people and the warm days in China.
passageZh:
3月19日 星期日：我现在在中国，打算骑车环游。中国很大，但美丽又有趣，我只想亲眼看看。
3月26日 星期日：今天很热，我弄丢了水壶，到路边一户人家求助。我不会说中文，可他们明白我的意思！他们给我水喝，还留我吃午饭。我多幸运！
4月13日 星期四：我现在在云南，这里是泼水节！人们庆祝傣历新年，互相泼水，因为这会给对方带来好运。能来到这里我多幸运！我会一直记得这里善良的人们和在中国温暖的日子。

title: Chinese Tea Culture
passage: China is the home of tea. Chinese people have drunk tea for thousands of years. Every region has its own famous tea. Longjing comes from Hangzhou, and Pu'er comes from Yunnan. When a guest visits a Chinese home, the host will often serve a cup of tea. The guest holds the cup with both hands as a sign of respect. My foreign friend, Anna, learnt this last month. She visited her classmate Xiao Ming's home for dinner. Mrs Wang, Xiao Ming's mum, brought out a small pot of green tea. "How fresh the smell is!" Anna said. Mrs Wang smiled and said, "In China, tea is not just a drink. It is a way to welcome friends." Anna watched carefully. She saw that the tea cup was small, and the tea was poured only half full. She asked why. Xiao Ming explained that in Chinese culture, a full cup means you want the guest to leave. Half a cup means care and friendship. Anna was surprised by these small but meaningful rules. She said, "How interesting your culture is!" Mrs Wang agreed: China is a beautiful and interesting place, and every custom has a story behind it.
passageZh: 中国是茶的故乡。中国人喝茶已有数千年历史。每个地区都有自己的名茶。龙井产自杭州，普洱产自云南。当客人拜访中国家庭时，主人常常会奉上一杯茶。客人双手捧杯，表示尊敬。我的外国朋友安娜上个月学到了这一点。她去同学小明家吃晚饭。小明的妈妈王太太端出一小壶绿茶。“这味道多清香啊！”安娜说。王太太笑着说：“在中国，茶不只是一种饮料。它是欢迎朋友的方式。”安娜仔细看着。她看到茶杯很小，茶只倒了半杯。她问为什么。小明解释说，在中国文化里，倒满杯意味着希望客人离开。半杯则代表关心和友谊。安娜对这些小而有意义的规矩感到惊讶。她说：“你们的文化多有趣啊！”王太太表示赞同：中国是一个美丽又有趣的地方，每一种习俗背后都有一个故事。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 6语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: The Lantern Festival
passage: The Lantern Festival is on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. It is the end of the Spring Festival celebrations. On that night, towns and parks are filled with colourful lanterns. What a beautiful sight it is! There are lanterns of all shapes: rabbits, dragons, fish and even cartoon characters. People write riddles on small pieces of paper and tie them to the lanterns. Visitors guess the riddles, and the right answers win small gifts. Food is an important part of the festival. People eat sweet rice balls called tangyuan. The round shape means family togetherness. Last year, our family went to the lantern show in the old town. My little sister ran from one lantern to another, pointing and laughing. How excited she was! My father took many photos. My mother bought a lantern shaped like a rabbit. We ate hot tangyuan while walking in the cold air. How warm the food felt inside! Many people say the Spring Festival is not truly over until the Lantern Festival ends. We love this festival, because it brings the whole family together under a sky of light.
passageZh: 元宵节在农历正月十五。它是春节庆祝活动的尾声。那一夜，城镇和公园里挂满了五彩的灯笼。多美的景象啊！灯笼有各种形状：兔子、龙、鱼，甚至还有卡通人物。人们把谜语写在小纸条上，系在灯笼上。游人猜谜语，猜中者赢得小礼物。食物是节日的重要部分。人们吃一种叫元宵的甜汤圆。圆圆的形状象征着全家团圆。去年，我们一家去老城看灯会。我妹妹从一个灯笼跑到另一个灯笼，又指又笑。她多兴奋啊！爸爸拍了很多照片。妈妈买了一个兔子形状的灯笼。我们在寒风里边走边吃热乎乎的元宵。这食物在体内多温暖啊！很多人说，元宵节结束，春节才算真正过完。我们爱这个节日，因为它把全家人聚在灯火之下。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 6语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: Meet the Panda Keeper
passage: Last Friday, our class visited the Chengdu Panda Base. We were lucky to meet Miss Zhou, a panda keeper. She has worked there for ten years. "What does a panda keeper do?" Daming asked. Miss Zhou smiled. She said, "We clean the enclosures, prepare fresh bamboo, and watch the pandas' health." She showed us a basket of fresh bamboo. "How much bamboo does a panda eat a day?" Lingling asked. "About twelve to thirty-eight kilograms," Miss Zhou answered. We were all surprised. Miss Zhou told us that pandas spend most of their day eating and sleeping. She also told us not to make loud noises or get too close. Pandas are shy animals. At noon, we watched a baby panda climb onto a wooden frame and then roll down. How cute it was! We all laughed. Miss Zhou said pandas are national treasures. Protecting them is a big job. She invited us to learn more about wildlife. Before leaving, we took a group photo with Miss Zhou. What a special day it was! We decided to read more books about animals and tell our friends to protect them.
passageZh: 上周五，我们班参观了成都熊猫基地。我们很幸运，见到了熊猫饲养员周小姐。她已经在那里工作十年了。“熊猫饲养员是做什么的？”大明问。周小姐笑了。她说：“我们打扫圈舍，准备新鲜竹子，观察熊猫的健康状况。”她给我们看了一篮子新鲜竹子。“熊猫一天吃多少竹子？”玲玲问。“大约十二到三十八公斤。”周小姐回答。我们都很惊讶。周小姐告诉我们，熊猫一天大部分时间都在吃和睡。她还告诉我们不要大声喧哗，也不要靠得太近。熊猫是胆小的动物。中午，我们看到一只熊猫宝宝爬上木架，然后又滚下来。它多可爱啊！我们都笑了。周小姐说，熊猫是国宝。保护它们是一项重大的工作。她邀请我们多了解野生动物。离开前，我们和周小姐合了影。多特别的一天啊！我们决定多读关于动物的书，并告诉朋友们保护动物。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 6语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: A Foreign Student in Beijing
passage: Peter is a fourteen-year-old boy from Canada. Last year, he came to Beijing as an exchange student. At first, everything was new and difficult. He could not read the Chinese menus, and he did not know how to take the subway. But his host family, the Chens, were very kind. Mrs Chen taught him to use chopsticks. Mr Chen took him to the Great Wall on a cool Saturday. "What a long wall it is!" Peter said, looking down from the watchtower. In Beijing, Peter tried many new things. He ate jianbing for breakfast, watched Beijing opera, and even learnt a few Chinese songs. He found that Chinese people were warm and helpful. When he got lost, a grandfather helped him find the right bus. Peter said, "How lucky I am to experience this culture!" At the end of the year, he could speak simple Chinese. He made many Chinese friends. Peter learned an important lesson: when you visit a new country, respect its customs, and the people will welcome you. When in Rome, do as the Romans do. Next year, Peter wants to bring his whole family to China.
passageZh: 彼得是一个十四岁的加拿大男孩。去年，他作为交换生来到北京。起初，一切都新鲜又困难。他看不懂中文菜单，也不会坐地铁。但他的寄宿家庭陈家人非常善良。陈太太教他用筷子。陈先生在一个凉爽的周六带他去了长城。“这墙多长啊！”彼得从瞭望塔往下看时说道。在北京，彼得尝试了许多新事物。他早餐吃煎饼，看京剧，甚至学了几首中文歌。他发现中国人热情又乐于助人。当他迷路时，一位老爷爷帮他找到了正确的公交车。彼得说：“能体验这种文化，我多幸运啊！”年底时，他已经能说简单的中文。他交了很多中国朋友。彼得学到了重要的一课：当你来到一个新国家，尊重它的习俗，人们就会欢迎你。入乡随俗。明年，彼得想带全家一起来中国。
source: 外研版（新标准·三起）；六上单元话题原创（参照教材Unit 6语法与话题，非教材原文）

title: At the Fast-food Restaurant
passage: Last Saturday, the children went to a fast-food restaurant near their school. Daming opened the door and said, "I am so hungry! Can I have a hamburger?" Lingling looked at the menu. "I want a hot dog, please," she said to the waiter. Amy wanted something healthy. "I'd like a vegetable salad and a glass of water," she said. Sam could not decide. The waiter smiled and asked, "What would you like, young man?" Sam thought for a moment. "I want a chicken burger and a cola," he said. The waiter wrote everything down carefully. Then Daming asked, "How much is it all together?" The waiter added the prices: the hamburger was four dollars, the hot dog three dollars, the salad five dollars, the chicken burger four dollars, and the colas were two dollars each. Daming took out his money. "It is eighteen dollars in all," he said. They found a table near the window. The food came quickly. Daming took a big bite and smiled. "This is the best hamburger ever!" he said. They enjoyed their meal and talked about their weekend plans.
passageZh: 上周六，孩子们去了学校附近的一家快餐店。大明推开门说：“我好饿！我能要一个汉堡包吗？”玲玲看着菜单。“请给我一个热狗。”她对服务员说。艾米想要健康一点的。“我想要一份蔬菜沙拉和一杯水。”她说。萨姆拿不定主意。服务员笑着问：“小朋友，你想要点什么？”萨姆想了一会儿。“我要一个鸡肉汉堡和一杯可乐。”他说。服务员仔细记下所有东西。然后大明问：“一共多少钱？”服务员算了算：汉堡包四美元，热狗三美元，沙拉五美元，鸡肉汉堡四美元，可乐每杯两美元。大明拿出钱。“一共十八美元。”他说。他们在窗边找了张桌子。食物很快端了上来。大明咬了一大口，笑了。“这是我吃过最好吃的汉堡！”他说。他们享受着这顿饭，聊着周末的计划。

title: The Waiter's Mistake
passage: One day, Mr and Mrs Green took their children to a new restaurant. The waiter came to their table with a big smile. "Good evening! What would you like?" he asked. Mr Green said, "I want a steak, please." Mrs Green said, "I'd like fish and chips." Their son Tom wanted a hamburger, and their daughter Lily wanted a bowl of noodles. The waiter repeated the order and went to the kitchen. Half an hour later, the food came. But something was wrong. Mr Green was given noodles instead of steak. Mrs Green got a hamburger, not fish. Tom found fish and chips in front of him, and Lily had a steak. The children looked at each other and started to laugh. Mr Green called the waiter politely. "Excuse me," he said, "but I think there is a small mistake." The waiter's face turned red. He checked the order again and said sorry many times. He took the food back and brought the correct dishes in ten minutes. To say sorry, he gave the family a free apple pie. It was delicious. The Greens left happily. They said even a mistake could end with a sweet surprise.
passageZh: 一天，格林夫妇带孩子们去一家新餐厅。服务员带着灿烂的微笑来到桌前。“晚上好！你们想吃点什么？”他问。格林先生说：“请给我一份牛排。”格林太太说：“我要炸鱼薯条。”他们的儿子汤姆想要一个汉堡包，女儿莉莉想要一碗面条。服务员重复了一遍点单，走进厨房。半小时后，食物端了上来。但出了点问题。给格林先生的是面条，而不是牛排。格林太太面前是汉堡包，而不是鱼。汤姆面前是炸鱼薯条，莉莉面前却是牛排。孩子们面面相觑，笑了起来。格林先生礼貌地叫住服务员。“打扰一下，”他说，“我想出了点小差错。”服务员的脸涨红了。他又核对了一遍点单，连连道歉。他把食物端回去，十分钟后送来了正确的菜。为了表示歉意，他送了这家人一份免费的苹果派。它非常美味。格林一家开心地离开了。他们说，即使是一个错误，也可能以甜蜜的惊喜结束。

title: Eating in an English Home
passage: Last winter, Daming stayed with an English family, the Smiths. On his first evening, Mrs Smith asked, "What would you like for dinner?" Daming did not know many English food words. He said, "I want rice, please." Mr Smith smiled. "We do not eat rice every day," he said. "Tonight, we will try fish and chips." When the food came, Daming saw white fish, golden chips and a bowl of peas. Mrs Smith asked, "How much salt would you like?" Daming was surprised. In China, the cook adds salt. In England, people put salt and vinegar on their own food. Daming tried a little vinegar on his chips. It tasted different, but not bad. For dessert, Mrs Smith made apple pie. "How much is a piece?" Daming asked by habit. The whole family laughed. "At home, we do not pay for dinner," Mrs Smith said. "It is free for you." Daming felt warm. He learnt that eating in a foreign home is not just about food. It is about sharing and kindness. Before he left, he wrote a thank-you card. On it, he drew a small panda.
passageZh: 去年冬天，大明住在英国家庭史密斯家。到他家的第一个晚上，史密斯太太问：“你晚餐想吃点什么？”大明不懂多少英国食物的词。他说：“请给我米饭。”史密斯先生笑了。“我们不是每天都吃米饭。”他说。“今晚，我们尝尝炸鱼薯条。”食物端上来时，大明看到了白鱼、金黄的薯条和一碗青豆。史密斯太太问：“你要多少盐？”大明很惊讶。在中国，厨师会加好盐。在英国，人们自己往食物上加盐和醋。大明在薯条上尝了一点醋。味道不同，但不难吃。甜点时，史密斯太太做了苹果派。“一块多少钱？”大明习惯性地问。全家人都笑了。“在家里，我们吃饭不付钱。”史密斯太太说。“对你来说是免费的。”大明心里暖暖的。他明白了，在外国人家吃饭不只是关于食物。它关乎分享与善意。离开前，他写了一张感谢卡。上面画了一只小熊猫。

title: The Menu at School
passage: Our school made a new menu this term, and it has both Chinese and Western food. On Monday, students can have rice with chicken and vegetables. On Tuesday, there are noodles and eggs. On Wednesday, the kitchen serves fish and potato soup. On Thursday, it is hamburgers and salad. On Friday, we have dumplings, which are everyone's favourite. The prices are low: rice dishes cost eight yuan, noodles six yuan, and hamburgers ten yuan. Every day, a bowl of free soup is ready near the door. Last week, Daming tried the hamburger for the first time. "How much is it?" he asked. The cook said ten yuan. Ten yuan was more than a rice dish, but Daming wanted to try it. He took a bite and said, "I want a hot dog next time!" Lingling chose the vegetable noodles. She said they were more delicious than she expected. Amy, who is from England, said the school dumplings tasted just like home. The school says the menu changes every month, so students will not get bored. Eating at school is not only about food. It is also about learning to choose healthy meals.

title: A Picnic by the Lake
passage: It was a sunny Saturday, and the children decided to have a picnic by the lake. They prepared the food at Daming's home first. Daming made ten sandwiches. Lingling cut some fruit into a big plate. Amy put juice and water bottles in the bag. Sam carried a thick blanket. When they arrived, they found a quiet place under a tall tree. Daming took out the sandwiches. "I want a chicken sandwich," Lingling said. "I want a tomato one," Amy said. Sam ate two sandwiches at once. Just as they started, a group of ducks swam near the bank. The ducks looked at the food with hungry eyes. Suddenly, one brave duck jumped onto the grass and tried to take a sandwich. The children laughed and moved the basket away. "The ducks want our food too!" Sam shouted. After lunch, they fed the ducks some bread pieces, not the sandwiches. The water was clear, and the sun was warm. They lay on the blanket and talked. Daming said, "A picnic is better than any restaurant." Everyone agreed. They packed the rubbish into a bag and left the place clean.

title: Our Weekend Plan
passage: Next Sunday is going to be a special day for our class. We are going to have a spring picnic in Renmin Park. Our teacher, Miss Wang, told us the plan on Friday. We are going to meet at the school gate at half past eight in the morning. Then we will take the bus to the park. When are we going to eat? We are going to have lunch at half past twelve. Each group is going to bring different food. Our group will make sandwiches and bring fruit. Another group is going to bring juice and cookies. Daming is going to take his new kite. The weather report says it will be sunny and warm on Sunday. It will not rain, and the wind will be soft. Miss Wang said we will play games after lunch. Sam hopes it will be a little windy, because he wants to fly his model plane. Lingling is going to take her notebook to draw the flowers. We are all excited. We will not forget to take a hat and a bottle of water. A good picnic needs good plans and good friends.

title: The Weather Tomorrow
passage: Good morning, everyone. Here is the weather report for tomorrow. In Beijing, it will be sunny in the morning, but it will turn cloudy in the afternoon. The temperature will be between fifteen and twenty-two degrees. In Shanghai, it will rain heavily in the morning. If you go out, please take an umbrella. The rain will stop in the evening. In Guangzhou, it will be hot and wet. The highest temperature will be thirty degrees. Children there will be able to swim, but please be careful. In Harbin, it will snow tomorrow. The ground will be white, and the temperature will fall to five below zero. People should wear thick coats and gloves. In Chengdu, the weather will be mild. It will be warm and dry, perfect for a walk. Remember, the weather changes quickly. We will update the report every six hours. Have a safe and happy day, no matter what the weather is like.

title: The Picnic That Was Saved
passage: Last Sunday, our class planned a picnic in the park. We were going to meet at eight o'clock. Daming made the sandwiches, and Lingling prepared the fruit. However, when Daming woke up, he looked out of the window. It was raining heavily. Black clouds covered the sky. Daming called Miss Wang at once. Miss Wang listened and said, "Don't worry. The radio says it will stop by ten. We are still going, but later." We waited at school. At ten o'clock, the rain stopped, and the sun came out. The ground was wet, but the air was fresh. We walked to the park and found a dry hill. We put our blankets down and opened the food. The ducks came again, but we were ready. After lunch, the sun shone warmly. Daming flew his kite high in the sky. Lingling drew the colourful flowers on the wet grass. We were going to go home at four, but we stayed until five. On the way back, Miss Wang said, "Plans may change, but a happy day is never wasted." We all agreed. That rainy start turned into the best picnic of the term.

title: Be Going to Help
passage: Next month, our class is going to do something meaningful. We are going to visit the Old People's Home near our school. Our teacher asked us to think about what we are going to do. Daming is going to play the suona for the grandparents. He has practised for two weeks. Lingling is going to read newspapers to those who cannot see well. Amy is going to sing English songs. The grandparents will be surprised and happy. Sam is going to help clean the rooms and wash the windows. Some students are going to make cards with beautiful wishes. We are going to meet at the school gate at nine o'clock on Saturday. We will take the bus together. We are going to leave the Old People's Home at twelve. We know the grandparents will be lonely without their own children around. We hope our visit will make them smile. Our teacher said, "When we give time and care, we will receive more love back." We are all looking forward to it. We will take small gifts, such as fruit and hand-made cards.

title: A Robot Weather Home
passage: In the future, our homes will be smarter. Scientists are making home robots that can predict the weather. Imagine: you wake up, and your robot says, "Good morning. It will rain at ten. Take your blue umbrella." You do not need to look at a phone. The robot will also tell you what to wear. If it is cold, it will lay a warm coat on your chair. If it is hot, it will prepare a bottle of cold water. But will robots replace real weather reports? Probably not. They will just make life easier. In our English class, we discussed what we are going to do with such a robot. Daming said he is going to ask the robot to wake him up five minutes earlier on rainy days. Lingling said she will ask the robot to water the plants when the soil is dry. Amy said robots will help old people who cannot go out easily. Sam said he hopes a robot will make his breakfast in the morning. We all laughed. The future is exciting, but we still need to plan our own days. Tools help us, but we make the choices.

title: A Sunny Day on the Farm
passage: It is a beautiful Saturday morning on Red Farm. The sun is shining warmly over the green fields. The birds are singing high up in the tall trees. Near the small river, the cows are drinking water slowly. Some ducks are swimming on the river, making little waves. Under the old apple tree, the farmer is feeding his chickens. The chickens are running around and making loud noises. On the soft grass, two little rabbits are jumping after a white butterfly. A brown dog is lying near the door, watching everything quietly. In the vegetable garden, a girl called Anna is picking red strawberries. Her brother Tom is helping her carry a small basket. Their mother is making sandwiches in the kitchen. Their father is repairing a broken fence near the road. Everyone is busy, but everyone is smiling. The farm is not noisy or crowded. It is calm and full of life. Anna stops for a moment and listens to the wind. She thinks this is the best morning of the whole year. On a farm, every day starts with the sun and ends with peace.

title: The Rainy Sunday
passage: It is Sunday, but the weather is not nice. The rain is falling heavily against the windows. The wind is blowing strongly outside. Many people are staying at home. A few birds are hiding under the roof of the garden shed. The street is empty, and the puddles are growing bigger. Tom looks out of the window and says, "We cannot go to the park today." Mum smiles and says, "But we can play board games together." She brings out a chess set. The family sits around the table. Even on a rainy day, a home can be warm and happy. title: The Messy Kitchen
passage: Daming walked into the kitchen after school. What a mess! The balloons were flying away to the ceiling. He and his mum had blown them up for his brother's birthday. On the floor, the apples were falling down the stairs. Daming had carried them from the market, but the bag broke on the last step. The cat was jumping onto the table, trying to catch a ball of string. A plate of eggs was rolling off the edge, and a glass of water was spilling onto the floor. Daming's little brother was sitting under the table, laughing loudly. "Why is everything going wrong today?" Daming asked himself. First, he caught the balloons and tied them to a chair. Then he picked up the apples, one by one. He put the eggs back into the box and mopped the water. The cat ran away with the string, and the cat was laughing at him, as if it were human. title: Daming's Suona Party
passage: It was Daming's birthday, and he decided to play the suona for his friends. He started to play a slow, beautiful song. The friends were listening quietly. But while he was playing the suona, the phone rang. Daming stopped and answered it. It was his aunt, asking about the party. After he put the phone down, he started again. He was playing the suona when the bell rang at the door. It was the milkman. Daming opened the door and said thank you. He went back and began for the third time. He was playing the suona happily when the dog started to bark loudly. The dog was afraid of the loud sound. Daming's father took the dog outside. Daming smiled and played once more. Just as he was reaching the end, it started to rain. The party had to move inside. Even with all the interruptions, Daming finished the song at last. His friends clapped and said it was the best suona they had ever heard. Daming learned that a real performer does not stop, no matter what happens.

title: Tom's Violin Practice
passage: Last Sunday, Tom decided to practise his violin at home. He was playing a slow, beautiful song when the doorbell rang. It was the postman, with a heavy parcel for his father. Tom carried the parcel into the study and went back to his music. He was playing again when the telephone rang loudly in the hall. It was his teacher, asking about the homework for Monday. After the call, Tom took a deep breath and started once more. He was playing the highest note when his baby sister woke up crying. Tom had to pick her up and walk around the room with her. When she finally fell asleep, Tom smiled and sat down again. He was playing his best piece when it started to rain heavily. The window was open, and rain was blowing onto his books. Tom jumped up and closed the window as fast as he could. By then, the sun was setting. Tom did not finish his practice that day, but he did not feel sad. His mother said life is full of little interruptions. What matters is that we keep trying, again and again.

title: The Cook Who Could Not Cook
passage: Sam wanted to cook a big dinner for his mother's birthday. He read a recipe and started bravely. He was cutting vegetables when the phone rang. His friend called to invite him to a football game. Sam said no, he had to cook. He went back to the kitchen. He was heating the soup when the doorbell rang. It was a delivery man with a parcel. Sam signed and closed the door. He was stirring the soup when his little brother ran in and knocked over a cup of water. The water spilled on the floor. Sam mopped it up and went back. He was just putting the noodles into boiling water when the smoke alarm beeped. The pan was too hot. He turned the heat down quickly. At last, the dinner was ready. It was not perfect, but it was warm. His mother tasted it and smiled. She said, "This is the best dinner, because you made it with love." Sam learned that cooking, like life, is full of small accidents, but care makes it right.

title: The Writer's Day
passage: Anna loved writing stories. Last Saturday, she decided to write a whole story in one day. She sat at her desk and opened her notebook. She was writing about a brave little robot when her mother called her for breakfast. After breakfast, she went back. She was writing when her brother asked her to help find his missing shoe. She helped, and the shoe was under the sofa. She returned to her desk. She was writing happily when the cat jumped onto the desk and sat on her notebook. Anna moved the cat gently and continued. She was just reaching the exciting ending when the doorbell rang. It was her grandma, bringing homemade cookies. Anna hugged her grandma and shared a cookie. In the evening, she finished the story. It was not as long as she hoped, but it was complete. Her father read it and said it was wonderful. Anna learned that a writer's life is full of breaks, but every break gives new ideas.

title: The Gardener
passage: Mr Lee loved his garden. Every spring, he planted tomatoes, carrots and sunflowers. Last Saturday morning, he decided to plant all the seeds. He was digging the soil when the phone rang. It was his old friend, inviting him to play chess. Mr Lee said he would call back. He went on digging. He was putting the seeds in the soil when it started to rain. He ran to fetch the cover for his plants. The rain stopped quickly, and the sun came out. He went back to work. He was watering the young plants when his neighbour came to chat. They talked for ten minutes about the weather. After the neighbour left, Mr Lee finished his work. He stood up and looked at the garden. It looked neat and full of hope. He knew the work would take many weekends. But every interruption gave him a rest. He smiled and went inside for a cup of tea. A garden teaches patience, he thought. Good things grow slowly, even when you are busy.

title: The Birthday Gift
passage: It was Daming's birthday yesterday. The house was full of family. His mum made a chocolate cake and put twelve candles on it. His grandparents came from the countryside. His aunt and uncle brought a big box with a red ribbon. Daming opened the box carefully and could not believe his eyes. Inside was a large model of the Shenzhou V spaceship. The name of the spaceship was written in gold letters. Daming read about Yang Liwei in his science book last month. In 2003, Yang Liwei became the first Chinese person in space. He spent about twenty-one hours there and came back safely. Daming's grandfather said that day made every Chinese person proud. Daming held the model gently and promised to look after it. He put it on his desk, where he could see it every morning. That night, he dreamed that he was flying above the earth. His teacher said science dreams often start with a small toy. Daming decided to read more books about space. Birthday gifts are nice, but a dream is even better.

title: The Space Lesson
passage: Last Monday, our science teacher gave us a special lesson about space. She showed us a video of Shenzhou V. In the video, Yang Liwei smiled at the camera and spoke to the whole nation. Our teacher told us that before the flight, Yang trained for many years. He exercised every day and learned how the spaceship worked. On 15 October 2003, the spaceship lifted off. It circled the earth fourteen times. Yang spent about twenty-one hours in space. When the spaceship landed in Inner Mongolia, people cheered and waved flags. Our teacher said that Yang was not alone. Thousands of scientists worked with him. She also told us about later spaceships. Now Chinese astronauts have stayed in space stations for months. title: The Model Rocket
passage: Daming loved his Shenzhou V model. He kept it on his desk. One Saturday, he decided to make a small rocket of his own. He used an empty bottle, paper and glue. He followed the steps carefully. First, he painted the bottle white. Next, he made a pointed top from red paper. Then, he stuck three small wings on the side. Finally, he wrote "CHINA" on the body. When he finished, the rocket looked just like a real spaceship, only smaller. Lingling came to see it. "Wow! It is wonderful," she said. Daming smiled. He wanted to launch it, but he knew a real engine was too dangerous. His father helped him make a soft launch with a string. They pulled the rocket up and let it fall gently. The children laughed as the rocket flew across the garden. Daming said, "One day, I will build a real rocket that can carry people." Lingling said, "Then take me with you!" Daming promised. Dreams begin with a small bottle and a lot of hope.

title: From a Toy to a Dream
passage: Many great scientists started with a simple toy. When Yang Liwei was a boy, he loved watching planes in the sky. He did not have a real spaceship, but he built model planes from wood and paper. He spent hours making them fly. Years later, his childhood love turned into a real career. Daming's story is similar. Recently, his aunt and uncle gave him the Shenzhou V model for his birthday. At first, it was just a toy on the desk. But Daming started to read about space. He watched videos of rocket launches. He drew pictures of spaceships in his notebook. He even joined the school science club. His teacher was surprised by his progress. She said, "You have changed from a boy who liked toys to a student who asks deep questions." Daming said the model was like a key. It opened a door to a new world. Now he wants to study science in middle school. He knows that real space travel needs hard work, not just dreams. But every great journey starts with one small step, or one small toy on a desk.

title: Two Great People
passage: Today we read about two famous people. The first is Yang Liwei, the astronaut. He spent about twenty-one hours in space in 2003. Before that, he was a pilot. He trained for years, and his body was tested again and again. When the spaceship lifted off, he was calm and brave. The second famous person is Helen Keller. She was born in America in 1880. When she was a baby, she became ill. After that, she couldn't see or hear. She lived in a dark and silent world. At first, she was often angry and sad. Then a teacher, Anne Sullivan, came to help her. Anne spelled words into Helen's hand. Slowly, Helen understood that everything had a name. Later, she went to college and became a writer. She travelled around the world to help disabled people. Both Yang and Helen had one thing in common: they did not give up. Their stories tell us that difficulties can become stepping stones. No matter what happens, a strong heart can light the way.

title: The Story of Helen Keller
passage: Helen Keller was a great writer. When she was nineteen months old, a fever made her unable to see or hear. She could not speak either, because she could not hear other people's voices. For years, she lived in a dark and silent world. She often got angry and kicked or screamed. Her parents did not know what to do. Then, when she was seven, a teacher named Anne Sullivan came. Anne loved Helen and was very patient. One day, she put Helen's hand under water. She spelled the word "W-A-T-E-R" into Helen's hand. At that moment, Helen understood. The cool water on her hand meant the word water. This was the key to learning. Helen worked very hard. She learned to read by touching raised letters. She learned to speak by feeling people's mouths. Later, she went to college and wrote many books. She travelled around the world and gave hope to millions of disabled people. Helen once said, "Keep your face to the sunshine, and you cannot see the shadow." Her life shows that even a dark world can be filled with light.

title: The First Chinese Astronaut
passage: Yang Liwei is a national hero. He was born in 1965, in Liaoning. As a boy, he loved planes and dreamed of flying. He studied hard and became a pilot in the air force. He flew for many years and was one of the best pilots in the country. In 1998, he was chosen to be an astronaut. The training was hard. He had to learn science, maths and how a spaceship worked. He also had to be strong enough to stand the heavy force at lift-off. For five years, he trained almost every day. On 15 October 2003, his dream came true. He flew into space in Shenzhou V. He spent about twenty-one hours in space. He circled the earth fourteen times. When the spaceship landed safely, the whole country cheered. Yang wrote a book about his experience. He told young people that space was not magic. It was the result of science and hard work. Today, more Chinese astronauts follow his steps. They live and work in space stations. Yang opened the door, and now others walk through it.
passageZh: 杨利伟是一位民族英雄。他1965年生于辽宁。小时候，他喜欢飞机，梦想飞翔。他努力学习，成为一名空军飞行员。他飞行多年，是全国最优秀的飞行员之一。1998年，他被选为宇航员。训练很艰苦。他必须学习科学、数学和飞船的工作原理。他还必须足够强壮，以承受升空时巨大的压力。五年里，他几乎每天都训练。2003年10月15日，他的梦想实现了。他乘坐神舟五号进入太空。他在太空度过了大约二十一个小时。他绕地球十四圈。当飞船安全着陆时，举国欢呼。杨利伟写了一本关于他经历的书。他告诉年轻人，太空不是魔法。它是科学和努力的结果。今天，更多中国宇航员追随他的脚步。他们在空间站里生活和工作。杨利伟打开了门，如今其他人走了进去。

title: A Blind Musician
passage: Many famous people turned their weaknesses into strengths. The great musician Beethoven began to lose his hearing when he was in his thirties. At first, he could not believe it. He loved music more than anything. How could a deaf man write music? He became very sad. But he did not give up. He kept composing. Even when he could not hear, he could feel the music in his heart. He put one end of a stick between his teeth and touched the piano with the other end. In this way, he felt the vibrations of the sound. Some of his greatest works came after he became deaf. His famous Ninth Symphony was written when he could not hear at all. At the first performance, the audience clapped and cried. Beethoven could not hear the applause. A young girl turned him around so he could see the smiling faces. Beethoven's story tells us that talent is not enough. Courage and hard work make a person great. Even when the world goes quiet, music can still play inside you.
passageZh: 许多名人把弱点变成了优势。伟大的音乐家贝多芬三十多岁时开始失去听力。起初，他无法相信。他爱音乐胜过一切。一个聋子怎么能写音乐呢？他非常难过。但他没有放弃。他继续作曲。即使他听不见，他仍能在心里感受音乐。他把一根棍子的一端咬在嘴里，另一端抵在钢琴上。这样，他就能感受到声音的振动。他一些最伟大的作品，都是在失聪后写的。他著名的《第九交响曲》，是在他完全听不见时写的。首演时，观众鼓掌落泪。贝多芬听不见掌声。一个小女孩把他转过来，让他看见笑脸。贝多芬的故事告诉我们，光有天赋不够。勇气和努力使人伟大。即使世界变得安静，音乐仍能在你心中奏响。
