title: The Boy Who Could Not Walk
passage: Stephen Hawking was one of the greatest scientists of our time. When he was twenty-one, doctors said he had a serious illness. They said he could not live long. His body became weaker and weaker. Soon he could not walk or move his arms. Later, he could not even speak. He had to sit in a wheelchair and use a special computer to talk. Many people would have given up. But Stephen loved thinking about the universe. He kept studying and writing books. His most famous book is A Brief History of Time. It sold millions of copies around the world. He travelled around the world to give talks. He met presidents and kings. He showed that a weak body can hold a powerful mind. When people asked him about his illness, he said he was lucky. He was lucky because his mind was still free. He told young people: remember to look up at the stars, not down at your feet. Stephen died in 2018, but his ideas live on. His story tells us that no difficulty is too big for a brave heart.

title: The Surprise Party Mistake
passage: It was Monday morning, and the students of Class 6 were acting strangely. When Miss Wang walked in, she stopped at the door. "Wait a minute," she said. "Why do you have cups on your heads? And Daming, why are you wearing a hat? It is not hot today." Daming smiled nervously. Lingling said, "It is a secret, Miss Wang." Miss Wang looked at Sam. "Sam, why is your face covered in flour?" Sam replied, "We wanted to make a surprise for you." The teacher sat down. "A surprise? What happened?" Daming explained. "We planned to make a birthday cake for you. We thought today was your birthday." Miss Wang laughed. "But my birthday is not until next month." Amy said, "We got the wrong date!" The teacher asked again, "And why do you have cups on your heads?" Lingling answered, "The cake fell on the floor, so we used the cups to catch the cream." The whole class waited. Miss Wang smiled warmly. "You are the naughtiest class, but also the sweetest. Let's clean up together, and next time check the date first!"

title: The Wrong Hats
passage: Last Friday, Class 6 had a very unusual morning. When the teacher walked in, she could not believe her eyes. Some children had paper cups on their heads. Others had flour on their noses and paint on their hands. The teacher stopped and asked why they looked so strange. At first, no one wanted to answer, because they felt shy. But while they were working, everything went wrong. A cup fell on Lingling's head and stuck in her hair. A bag of flour broke and flew all over Sam's face. title: Why Are You Wearing Rain Boots?
passage: One wet Monday, Daming came to school in rain boots. It had rained at the weekend, but the sun was out now. Lingling looked at his feet. "Daming, why are you wearing rain boots? It is not raining." Daming smiled. "I have a reason," he said. Sam looked down and noticed something. "Daming, why is your left boot green and your right boot blue?" Daming's face turned red. He hid Daming's shoes and put two different boots by his bed. In the morning, Daming was half asleep and put them on without looking. The paper on his back was a note his brother stuck there. It said, "Good morning, big brother!" The whole class laughed. Even Daming laughed. Miss Wang said, "Now we know why you look so strange." title: The Big Mistake in the Kitchen
passage: Mrs Green asked her son Tom to wash the tomatoes for dinner. Tom took the tomatoes to the kitchen. But he came back five minutes later with a worried face. "Mum, why are the tomatoes soft? Did I do something wrong?" Mrs Green went to the kitchen. She looked at the bowl and started to laugh. Tom had put the tomatoes in a pot of hot water, because he thought he was washing potatoes. The tomatoes were now warm and soft. Mrs Green said, "Tom, why did you use hot water?" Tom said, "You washed potatoes in hot water yesterday. I thought all vegetables were the same." Mrs Green smiled. "Tomatoes are softer than potatoes. You only need to wash them in cool water." Tom felt silly, but his mother did not blame him. She said, "Mistakes are how we learn. Now you will remember." They made tomato soup with the soft tomatoes. It tasted delicious. Tom learned that different things need different care. The next time, he checked before he acted.

title: The Empty Gift Box
passage: It was the last day of school before the holidays. Daming had a small box for his teacher. He carried it carefully all morning. At break time, Lingling asked, "Daming, why are you hiding that box behind your back? What is inside?" Daming said, "It is a gift for Miss Wang. Do not open it." But when Daming went to the washroom, Sam could not wait. He opened the box quietly. There was nothing inside! Sam was very surprised. When Daming came back, Sam asked, "Why is the box empty? Did you forget the gift?" Daming smiled. "The gift is not inside the box. It is the box itself. I made it myself, and I am going to put a paper flower inside after school." Lingling laughed. "You made us all curious!" Miss Wang heard the story. She said, "A gift that makes people smile even before they open it is the best kind." Daming gave her the box with the paper flower in the end. Miss Wang put it on her desk, where it still sits today.

title: The Yearbook Project
passage: The end of primary school is coming soon. Our class decided to make a yearbook for everyone. We talked about what to write. First, we can write best wishes to each friend. Daming said, "To Amy: wishing you happiness every day." Lingling said, "To Sam: good luck in your new middle school." We also wanted to write to our teacher. "Thank you for helping us, Miss Wang." Daming said he would keep them forever. We know we may not see each other every day. But we can send emails and meet on holidays. We wrote our names on the last page. We also wrote our telephone numbers and emails. Best wishes to you, my dear friends. This yearbook will be our favourite memory. We will look at it again in ten years and smile.

title: The Last Week
passage: It was the last week of primary school, and the classroom felt different. The walls were covered with colourful cards and drawings. Every student prepared a special book for the others to sign. Lingling opened her book and wrote to Daming first. She wished him happiness every day and success in the future. Daming wrote back that he would never forget their football games. Amy drew a small star and wished her Chinese friends good luck. Sam wrote a funny joke, and the whole group laughed loudly. Their teacher, Miss Wang, also wrote a long message. She said she was proud of them and would miss them all. Some children felt happy, but many had tears in their eyes. They knew that in September they would go to different schools. They promised to keep in touch by email and video calls. They agreed to meet every summer holiday in the old playground. Lingling put a group photo on the first page of her book. She wrote the date under it: a day she would remember forever. Best wishes are like seeds; if you keep them, they grow.

title: A Message to My Best Friend
passage: Dear Daming, we have been friends for six years. We sat next to each other in Grade Three. I still remember you shared your lunch with me when I forgot my box. You were always the first to help. Now we are going to different middle schools. You will go to Red Star, and I will go to No.1 Middle School. It may be hard to see each other every day. But I will never forget the days we played football after class. We laughed, we ran, and we sometimes fell down together. You are the kindest person I know. I wish you happiness every day. I wish you good luck in your studies. I hope you make many new friends, but please remember me. We can meet on Saturdays, and we can write emails every week. Best wishes to you, my dear friend. When we grow up, I want us to meet again and talk about our school days. Yours, Lingling.

title: The Teacher's Farewell
passage: On the last day, Miss Wang stood in front of the class. She looked at each student slowly. "Boys and girls," she said, "these six years have been the happiest part of my work." The classroom was quiet. She continued. "When you came to Grade Three, you were small and shy. Now you are tall and confident. I have watched you grow." She turned to Daming. "Daming, your suona music made our festivals special." Then she smiled at Lingling. "Lingling, your drawings made our classroom beautiful." She looked at Amy and Sam. "Amy, your English songs touched us. Sam, your courage in sports inspired us." Miss Wang's eyes were wet. "You are going to different schools now. You will face new tests and new challenges. Remember to be kind, to work hard, and to never give up." The class stood up and clapped. Some students cried. Daming shouted, "Thank you, Miss Wang! We will come back to see you." Miss Wang nodded. "Best wishes to you all. I will wait for your news." Best wishes are short sentences that carry warm feelings to our closest friends.

title: The Gift of a Memory Book
passage: When Anna was ten, her grandmother gave her a memory book. It was a simple blue book. Grandma said, "Write down the happy moments. Years later, you will read them and smile." Anna wrote her first story: a picnic with her family. She stuck a photo inside. Every month, she added a page. She wrote about her birthday, a school trip, and a funny day with her friends. Years passed. Anna grew up, finished school, and went to a new city. One day, she found the old blue book in a box. She opened it slowly. The first photo showed a little girl with a big smile. She read her own childish writing. She laughed out loud. In that moment, she felt as if she were ten again. She thought of Grandma, who had passed away. The book was like a hug from the past. Anna decided to start a new memory book for her own children. She understood what Grandma meant. Best wishes and happy memories are the gifts that last. They cost nothing, but they are priceless.

title: Going to Different Schools
passage: When June came, the Grade Six students started to think about autumn. They were going to different middle schools across the city. Daming would study at Red Star Middle School, which had a science club. Lingling would walk to No.1 Middle School, next to a small library. Amy was returning to London, where she would learn French. Sam was going to join the football team at Greenfield School. During the last week, the students shared their future plans. Daming said he was going to study Computer Science and robotics. Lingling said she was going to read more history books. Amy said she would keep practising Chinese, because she loved it. Sam said he wanted to be both a student and a sports star. Some students felt excited, but others felt a little worried. Their teacher told them that change was not something to fear. New schools would bring new teachers, new books and new friends. The class promised to remember the happy days they shared. They exchanged phone numbers and home addresses. On the last day, they hugged and said goodbye with smiles. Different schools, different dreams, but the same warm memories.

title: What Are You Going to Study?
passage: On the last Monday, Miss Wang asked each student one question: "What are you going to study in middle school?" Daming stood up first. "I am going to study Computer Science. I love building small robots." Lingling went next. "I am going to study Chinese, History and Geography. I want to learn more about our country." Amy said, "In England, we will study many subjects. I am going to keep Chinese, because it is useful and beautiful." Sam laughed. "I am going to study PE, of course. But I will also work hard on maths." The teacher nodded. She told them that middle school had more subjects than primary school. They would meet new teachers and new friends. They would have homework, tests and after-school activities. It might be hard at first, but they would get used to it. "We are going to different schools," Daming said quietly. "Yes," said Miss Wang, "but you are all going to grow." The class took a group photo after the talk. They promised to meet once a year and share their new stories.
passageZh: 在最后一个周一，王老师问每个学生一个问题：“你们打算在中学学什么？”大明先站起来。“我打算学习计算机科学。我爱做小机器人。”玲玲接着说：“我打算学语文、历史和地理。我想更多地了解我们的国家。”艾米说：“在英国，我们会学很多科目。我打算继续学中文，因为它有用又美丽。”萨姆笑了。“我当然要学体育。但我也会努力学数学。”老师点点头。她告诉他们，中学的科目比小学多。他们会遇到新老师、新朋友。他们会有作业、考试和课外活动。起初可能很难，但他们会习惯的。“我们要去不同的学校了。”大明轻声说。“是的，”王老师说，“但你们都会成长。”谈话结束后，全班合了影。他们约定每年聚一次，分享各自的新故事。

title: Daming's New School
passage: Daming will study at Red Star Middle School in September. He visited the school with his parents last month. The school gate was wide and modern. There were tall teaching buildings, a large playground and a small garden. Inside the science building, Daming saw a robotics room. On the walls, there were photos of student robots. His future teacher, Mr Zhao, came to meet them. He told Daming that the school had won many science prizes. Daming's eyes lit up. Mr Zhao said, "If you work hard, you can join our robotics team." Daming promised to practise over the summer. On the way home, he felt both excited and a little nervous. He would miss his old classmates. But he also wanted to make new friends. He thought about his primary school days. They had been happy, but it was time to move on. He wrote in his notebook: "New school, new books, new dreams. I am ready." That night, he put his Shenzhou V model on his school bag. It was like a lucky friend for the journey ahead.
passageZh: 大明九月将在红星中学学习。上个月，他和父母参观了学校。校门宽敞而现代。那里有高高的教学楼、一个大操场和一个小花园。在科学楼里，大明看到了一个机器人实验室。墙上挂着学生机器人的照片。他未来的老师赵老师来见他们。他告诉大明，学校赢得过许多科学奖项。大明的眼睛亮了。赵老师说：“如果你努力，就能加入我们的机器人队。”大明答应暑假里练习。回家的路上，他既兴奋又有点紧张。他会想念老同学。但他也想交新朋友。他想起小学生活。那些日子很快乐，但也是时候向前走了。他在笔记本上写道：“新学校、新书、新梦想。我准备好了。”那天晚上，他把神舟五号模型放在书包上。它就像陪伴前路的幸运朋友。

title: Amy Is Going Back to London
passage: Amy was an exchange student from London. She had studied in China for two years. Now it was time to go home. On her last week, she said goodbye to every place. She visited the small noodle shop near the school. She walked around the panda park with Daming. She gave Lingling a British doll as a gift. The Chinese students gave her a book of Chinese stories in English. At the goodbye party, Amy sang a Chinese song. Everyone clapped. Daming said, "We're going to different schools, but we will write emails." Amy smiled. She said, "I will keep practising Chinese. When I come back, I want to speak it well." Lingling said, "We will miss you." Amy's eyes were wet. She said, "Thank you for two wonderful years. China is now a second home to me." On the day she left, the whole class went to the airport. They waved until the plane was out of sight. Amy promised to return. Different countries, different languages, but friendship stays the same.
passageZh: 艾米是一位来自伦敦的交换生。她在中国学习了两年。现在是时候回家了。最后一周，她和每个地方道别。她去了学校附近的小面馆。她和大明逛了熊猫公园。她送给玲玲一个英国娃娃作为礼物。中国学生送她一本英文版的中国故事书。在告别聚会上，艾米唱了一首中文歌。大家鼓掌。大明说：“我们要去不同的学校了，但我们会写邮件。”艾米笑了。她说：“我会继续练中文。等我回来，我想说得流利。”玲玲说：“我们会想你的。”艾米的眼睛湿润了。她说：“谢谢你们这美好的两年。中国现在是我的第二个家。”她离开那天，全班都去了机场。他们挥手，直到飞机消失在视线里。艾米承诺会回来。不同的国家，不同的语言，但友谊不变。

title: Ready for Middle School
passage: The summer after Grade Six is an important time. It is not just a holiday. It is a bridge between primary and middle school. Many students use the summer to get ready. Daming bought new pens, a schoolbag and a maths exercise book. He also read two science books. Lingling visited the city library near her new school. She wanted to know the way, so she would not get lost on the first day. Sam practised football every morning, because he wanted to join the school team. Amy read Chinese stories to keep up her Chinese. Some students feel worried about the new school. They worry about harder lessons, new teachers and making friends. But their parents told them that everyone feels the same at first. The key is to be brave and ask for help when you need it. In September, they will walk through the school gate with new books and big hopes. Middle school is not an end. It is a new beginning. Different schools, different dreams, but the same bright future waiting for every student.
passageZh: 六年级后的夏天是一段重要时光。它不只是一个假期。它是连接小学和中学的桥梁。许多学生利用暑假做准备。大明买了新笔、一个书包和一本数学习题册。他还读了两本科学书。玲玲参观了新学校附近的市图书馆。她想认认路，这样第一天就不会迷路。萨姆每天早上练足球，因为他想进校队。艾米读中文故事，保持中文水平。有些学生对新学校感到担心。他们担心功课更难、新老师和交朋友。但父母告诉他们，起初每个人都会有同样的感觉。关键是要勇敢，需要时就求助。九月，他们将带着新书和大大的希望，走进校门。中学不是终点。它是一个新的开始。不同的学校，不同的梦想，但同样光明的未来，等待着每一个学生。

title: 开学第一天
passage: It is the first day of junior high school. In the morning, Lily meets her new classmate Tom at the school gate. "Hi!" says Lily. "Hello!" Tom answers with a big smile. "Good morning," says Lily. "How are you?" "I'm fine, thank you. Nice to meet you," says Tom. "Nice to meet you too," Lily says. "What's your name?" asks Tom. "My name is Lily. What's your name?" "I'm Tom." They walk to the classroom together and talk happily.

title: Finding Lost Items
passage: It was Monday morning. Tom arrived at school and found his schoolbag was messy. He looked inside and saw many things. 'What do I have in my schoolbag?' he thought. There were some books under a blue bottle, three red rulers in the bag, and a small eraser on top of everything. Tom was looking for his keys because he needed to open his locker. Suddenly, he found them next to the eraser. 'Thank you for helping me find them,' Tom said to his friend Lily. 'You're welcome,' Lily replied with a smile. Tom felt happy because he had found all his things.

title: 欢迎新朋友
passage: Last Sunday morning, Tom visited his uncle's farm. In the yard, he saw many animals. 'What are those?' Tom asked. His uncle smiled and said, 'They are geese.' Tom counted the geese and found there were five. After that, his uncle gave him a carrot. 'Look at this carrot,' said his uncle. 'It's fresh and good for you.' Tom thought it would be fun to feed the animals. He gave a piece of carrot to each goose. One goose ate it quickly and looked for another piece. Tom enjoyed feeding the geese very much. It was a wonderful day at the farm.

passage: My school is a modern building with many special places. At the back of the school, there is a large sports field where we do exercises every morning. title: 我的最爱科目
passage: My name is Lily, and I'm in Grade 7. This term, my favourite subject is biology. I find it exciting because it helps me understand life and how things work. In class, we learn about plants, animals, and even the human body. I'm good at remembering scientific facts, and I want to be a scientist in the future. My teacher is excellent at explaining difficult ideas. She often uses experiments to make learning more interesting. Both geography and history are useful too, but biology is the most exciting for me. I hope to learn more about magic in nature next term.

passage: Last week, our school held a club fair. I was interested in joining a club but couldn't decide which one. There were many options: drama club, music club, and nature club. title: 我的日常生活
passage: My name is Li Ming, and I'm a student from Finland. My daily routine usually starts at 6:30 a.m. when I get up. I brush my teeth and take a shower before having breakfast. After that, I prepare my school bag and go to school. At school, I have different classes like math, science, and home economics. I finish my classes at around 3:30 p.m. and then do my homework. Sometimes I play ice hockey with my friends after school. In the evening, I usually read books or help my parents with housework. I go to bed at 9:30 p.m. On weekends, I stay at home and make use of the time to relax. My daily routine is busy but interesting.

passage: Last Saturday was my best friend Lily's birthday. I wanted to give her a special surprise, so I contacted her parents to plan something meaningful. They told me her birthday was on 2nd August, and she would be turning thirteen. I decided to organize a small celebration at her home. I bought a chocolate cake, some colorful balloons, and her favorite pizza. When Lily came home, we turned off the lights and I made her blow out the candles on the cake. She was so surprised and happy! We took photos and enjoyed the party together. It was one of the best birthdays I've ever celebrated.

passage: Last Sunday, I visited the zoo with my family. I was excited to see many animals there. My favorite animal was the giraffe because it has a very long neck. However, I felt quite sad when I learned that some animals are in danger. For example, elephants are hunted for their ivory, and forests where many animals live are being cut down. I think we should all take care of these beautiful creatures. They are our friends and we need to save them from danger.

title: Finding My Badminton Racket
passage: Last Tuesday after school, I went to the sports hall to play badminton with my friends. I put my T-shirt and my badminton racket on a mat, but when I returned, they were gone! I asked a few students if they saw them, but no one knew. Then I noticed a blue rope near the door and thought maybe someone took my things by mistake. Just as I was about to leave, Han Lin came over with my racket and T-shirt. 'Is this yours?' he asked. 'Yes, that's mine! Thank you so much,' I replied. I felt so relieved to have my things back. We then played a doubles match, and even though we lost, I had a great time with my friends.
passageZh: 上周二放学后，我去体育馆和朋友们打羽毛球。我把我的T恤和羽毛球拍放在垫子上，但当我回来时，它们不见了！我问了几个学生是否看到它们，但没人知道。然后我注意到门附近有一根蓝色的绳子，心想也许有人误拿了我的东西。正当我准备离开时，韩林拿着我的T恤和球拍走了过来。'这是你的吗？'他问道。'是的，那是我的！非常感谢，'我回答道。找回我的东西后，我感到非常放松。然后我们进行了一场双打比赛，虽然我们输了，但我和朋友们玩得很开心。

title: Healthy Eating Habits
passage: Li Hua is a middle school student who loves eating fast food. After all, it's convenient and tasty. Among his favorite meals are hamburgers and fish and chips. However, his mother is worried because Li Hua is getting a bit fat. She reads an article about healthy eating habits and decides to help him improve his diet. Instead of having fast food for dinner, she now cooks balanced meals with vegetables like cabbage, beans, and onions. Li Hua was not happy at first, but after trying the new dishes, he started to feel healthier. His mother also adds a pear or some salad to his meal. Now, Li Hua has a better habit of eating well and feels more energetic every day.
passageZh: 李华是一名中学生，他喜欢吃快餐。毕竟，快餐既方便又美味。他最喜欢的食物包括汉堡包和炸鱼薯条。然而，他的妈妈很担心，因为李华有点胖了。她读了一篇关于健康饮食习惯的文章，决定帮助他改善饮食。她不再让李华吃晚饭时吃快餐，而是用卷心菜、豆类和洋葱等蔬菜制作均衡的饭菜。起初李华不高兴，但尝试了新菜肴后，他开始感觉更健康了。妈妈还在他的餐点中加入一个梨或一些沙拉。现在，李华有了更好的饮食习惯，每天感觉更有活力了。

title: Dragon Festival Celebrations
passage: It's a bright Saturday morning and I'm at the central market with my family. The market is colourful with many people buying decorations for the Dragon Boat Festival. My mother is looking at some beautiful paintings of dragons while my father is talking to a passenger about the festival races. At the moment, I'm helping my little sister choose a shuttlecock to play with later. We are side by side, looking forward to the festival activities. My phone rings suddenly. It's my friend Lily. She asks, 'What are you doing right now?' I explain that I'm at the market and will call her back after we finish shopping. The market is busy with people rushing around, but we're not in a hurry. We want to enjoy every moment of this special day.

title: Mountain Weather Adventure
passage: Last weekend, Tom and his family went hiking in the mountains. At the start, the weather was perfect with blue skies and sunshine. Although they felt tired after climbing for two hours, they were in high spirits. Suddenly, grey clouds appeared at the top of the mountain. It began to rain heavily, so they found a rest area to take shelter. Because of the bad weather, they couldn't reach the peak as planned. However, Tom felt lucky to experience such magical mountain weather. At the end of the day, even though their clothes were wet, they made good progress and enjoyed the adventure.
passageZh: 上周末，汤姆和他的家人去山里远足。开始时天气完美，天空湛蓝阳光明媚。虽然爬了两小时后他们感到疲惫，但情绪高涨。突然，灰色的云出现在山顶。开始下大雨，所以他们找到一个休息区躲避。因为天气不好，他们无法按计划到达山顶。然而，汤姆觉得自己很幸运能体验到这样神奇的山区天气。那天结束时，尽管衣服湿了，但他们取得了很好的进展并享受了这次冒险。

title: 难忘的博物馆之旅
passage: Last Friday, our class went on a school trip to the science museum. We explored different exhibitions and learned many interesting things. There was a special space exhibition with robots that could talk and answer questions. I certainly enjoyed seeing those machines work. Later, we visited a wastewater plant near the museum. We saw how they remove germs from water through different steps with special machines. It was amazing to see the whole process from dirty water to clean water. Finally, our teacher asked us to write a diary entry about what we saw and learned. I filled my notebook with notes and drawings. It was a day to remember!
passageZh: 上周五，我们班级去科学博物馆进行了一次学校旅行。我们探索了不同的展览，学到了很多有趣的东西。有一个特别的太空展览，里面有能够说话和回答问题的机器人。我肯定很喜欢看那些机器人的运作。后来，我们参观了博物馆附近的一个污水处理厂。我们看到了他们如何通过特殊的机器和不同的步骤去除水中的微生物。看到从脏水到净水的整个过程真是太神奇了。最后，老师要求我们写一篇日记，记录我们看到和学到的东西。我用笔记和图画填满了我的笔记本。这是难忘的一天！

title: The Emperor's New Clothes
passage: Once upon a time, there was an emperor who loved beautiful clothes. He spent all his money on new outfits and forgot about his kingdom. Two artists came to the city and pretended to make special clothes only for him. 'Did you hear about the emperor's new clothes?' people asked each other. 'Yes, I did. They are magical!' others replied. The emperor was afraid at first, but he decided to visit the artists. They showed him an empty net and praised the invisible clothes. The emperor pretended to see the beautiful clothes and walked through the city in his underwear. Everyone laughed at him except one little child who said, 'But he has nothing on!'
passageZh: 从前，有一位皇帝非常喜欢漂亮的衣服。他把所有的钱都花在新衣服上，忘记了王国的事。两个艺术家来到城里，假装为他制作特殊的衣服。'你听说皇帝的新衣服了吗？'人们互相询问。'是的，我听说了。它们是神奇的！'其他人回答。起初皇帝很害怕，但他决定去见艺术家。他们向他展示了一张空网，称赞那些看不见的衣服。皇帝假装看到了美丽的衣服，穿着内衣在城里走动。所有人都嘲笑他，除了一个小孩说：'但他什么都没穿！'

title: 云南假期之旅
passage: Last summer, I went on holiday to Yunnan with my family. We stayed in a comfortable hotel near the countryside. One morning, we visited a famous palace in the city center. The palace was beautiful, with colorful artwork on the walls. During our trip, we also saw some deer in the forest near our hotel. I took many photos of them in the sun. In the afternoon, we walked through a large square and enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere. I even tried playing an accordion that a street musician was playing. It was not easy, but I had fun trying something new. The holiday was probably the best one I've ever had because I got to experience both nature and culture.
passageZh: 去年夏天，我和家人一起去了云南度假。我们住在乡下附近的一家舒适的旅馆里。一天早上，我们参观了市中心的一座著名宫殿。宫殿很漂亮，墙上挂着色彩缤纷的艺术品。旅行期间，我们还看到了旅馆附近森林里的一些鹿。我在阳光下给它们拍了很多照片。下午，我们穿过一个大型广场，享受着宁静的氛围。我还尝试弹奏了一位街头音乐家演奏的手风琴。这并不容易，但我尝试新事物玩得很开心。这次假期可能是我经历过的最好的假期，因为我既能体验自然又能感受文化。

title: 新家的第一天
passage: Last weekend, my family moved to a new apartment in our community. It was a long journey from our old home, but we felt joy when we arrived. My bedroom was almost empty, so I decided to decorate it with photos from my old room. 'Could you please help me hang up these pictures?' I asked my mum. 'Sure,' she replied. We spent the afternoon packing up my things and arranging furniture. On the balcony, my dad and I put some flowers on the table to add color to our new living room. 'Ah, this looks familiar already,' I said with a smile. By evening, our new home felt comfortable and warm.
passageZh: 上周末，我们全家搬到了社区的一个新公寓。从旧家搬来是一段漫长的旅程，但到达时我们感到很开心。我的卧室几乎是空的，所以我决定用旧房间的照片来装饰它。'你能帮我挂这些照片吗？'我问妈妈。'当然，'她回答。我们花了一下午打包我的东西和摆放家具。在阳台上，爸爸和我把一些花放在桌上，为我们的新客厅增添色彩。'啊，这看起来已经有点熟悉了，'我笑着说。到了晚上，我们的新家感觉舒适又温暖。

title: 不同但友好的新朋友
passage: Last Monday, I met a new student named Tom at school. We were alone in the classroom when he accidentally knocked over my books. I was a bit angry at first, but then I noticed his honest expression. Tom is hard-working and outgoing, with a great sense of humour. Besides, we have many interests in common, like reading novels and playing the flute. The teacher asked us to compare our daily routines. title: 大自然的奇妙
passage: Last Sunday, I visited the nature museum with my classmates. It was amazing to see so many plants and animals there. The African elephant caught my attention immediately because it is the biggest land animal in the world. Actually, I believe the most interesting animal was the cheetah, which runs the fastest among all land animals. In the plant section, bamboo appeared to be very useful. For this reason, I think bamboo is perhaps the most useful plant in the world. The museum also had a special area showing how plants and animals are connected in an ecosystem. I learned that bees help with pollination by carrying pollen from one flower to another. It was a wonderful day that made me understand the importance of nature.

title: 未来梦想家
passage:
Last week, our school had a special guest visit. Mr. Johnson, a famous futurist, came to talk about what the future might be like. He mentioned that in the future, people might live to be over 100 years old thanks to medical advances. 'Will most people live in outer space?' someone asked. 'No, they won't,' Mr. Johnson answered, 'but cities will become more efficient with better technology.'

During the Q&A session, I challenged him about the future of education. 'What will happen to traditional schools?' I questioned. He smiled and said, 'Education will depend more on creativity and emotional intelligence than just memorization.' His words made me think about my own future. I hope I can become an expert in medical research to help find cures for diseases like cancer. With hard work, I believe dreams can come true.
passageZh:
上周，我们学校有一位特别的客人来访。约翰逊先生，一位著名的未来学家，来谈论未来可能是什么样子。他提到，未来人们可能活到100岁以上，这得益于医学的进步。'大多数人会住在外太空吗？'有人问。'不，他们不会，'约翰逊先生回答，'但城市会变得更高效，拥有更好的技术。'

在问答环节，我向他挑战关于教育的未来。'传统学校会发生什么？'我问道。他微笑着说，'教育将更多地取决于创造力和情绪智力，而不仅仅是记忆。'他的话让我思考我自己的未来。我希望我能成为医学研究专家，帮助找到像癌症这样的疾病的治愈方法。通过努力工作，我相信梦想可以实现。

title: 化解友谊危机
passage: Last week, I had a big argument with my best friend Lily over a misunderstanding. We were both nervous and didn't talk for three days. Finally, I decided to pay attention to my feelings and write her a letter. If you want to solve the problem, a face-to-face talk usually works the best, but I was too nervous to meet in person. In my letter, I carefully explained my side of the story and apologized for my impolite words. The next day, Lily called me and said she received my message. We agreed to meet at the school hall after class. When we saw each other face to face, we both felt calm again. We made up and promised to communicate better in the future. This experience taught me that communication can benefit our relationships if we stay calm and express ourselves clearly.

title: 暴风雨中的救援
passage: Last Saturday, I was visiting my grandparents in their neighbourhood when a heavy rainstorm suddenly hit. The rain was pouring down so hard that floodwater began to rise quickly on the streets. As soon as I noticed the danger, I called the firefighters for help. While we were waiting, I saw a schoolgirl struggling in the floodwater near her home. Without hesitation, I jumped in and rescued her just before the water reached her roof. By the time the firefighters arrived, we were both out of breath but safe. The girl's relatives came to thank me, and I felt like a hero. This experience taught me the importance of being prepared for natural disasters.

title: 文化差异的体验
passage: Last summer, I had an interesting cultural exchange with an Indian student named Priya. When we first met, I bowed to her as a greeting. Priya looked confused and said, 'In India, we usually just say hello or shake hands.' I was embarrassed because I thought bowing was proper. Priya explained that bowing is too formal for casual meetings in her culture. We then talked about different customs. She told me that in India, people often eat curry with their hands, while I use chopsticks. I found these cultural differences fascinating but sometimes confusing. Priya taught me how to use chopsticks correctly, and I showed her how to bow properly. By the end of our meeting, we got along well and learned from each other. We both agreed that understanding different cultures can go a long way in making friends.
passageZh: 去年夏天，我有一位名叫普丽娅的印度学生进行了一次有趣的文化交流。当我们初次见面时，我向她鞠躬致意。普丽娅看起来很困惑，说：'在印度，我们通常只是说你好或握手。'我感到很尴尬，因为我认为鞠躬是合适的。普丽娅解释说，在她的文化中，鞠躬对于非正式的会面太过正式。然后我们讨论了不同的习俗。她告诉我，在印度，人们经常用手吃咖喱，而我用筷子。我发现这些文化差异很有趣但有时令人困惑。普丽娅教我如何正确使用筷子，而我向她展示了如何正确鞠躬。在我们会面的结束时，我们相处得很好，并互相学习。我们都认为，理解不同的文化在交朋友方面大有帮助。

title: 图书馆的冒险之旅
passage: Last Friday, our class had a special reading activity in the school library. I was looking for a good read for my book report when I met our librarian, Ms. Wang. She recommended Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, a famous fantasy novel. 'Have you decided on a book for your report?' she asked with a gentle smile. I nodded and replied, 'Yes, I have. I've just borrowed it from the library.' As I was reading, I got lost in the wonderful world of Wonderland, where Alice met strange characters and experienced amazing adventures. The story has a perfect build-up leading to an exciting climax. I consider this book one of the most inspiring literary works I've ever read. My friend Tom has never heard of this book before, but after I told him about it, he became very interested and decided to read it too.
passageZh: 上周五，我们班在学校图书馆举办了一次特别的阅读活动。我正在为我的读书报告寻找一本好书时，遇到了我们的图书管理员王女士。她向我推荐了《爱丽丝梦游仙境》，这是一本著名的幻想小说。'你决定好读书报告要读的书了吗？'她温柔地微笑着问道。我点点头回答：'是的，我已经决定了。我刚从图书馆借了这本书。'当我阅读时，我完全沉浸在奇妙的爱丽丝仙境世界中，在那里爱丽丝遇到了奇怪的角色并经历了令人惊叹的冒险。这个故事有完美的铺垫，引向一个激动人心的高潮。我认为这本书是我读过的最具启发性的文学作品之一。我的朋友汤姆以前从未听说过这本书，但在我告诉他之后，他变得非常感兴趣，并决定也去读一读。

title: Volunteer Experience
passage: I have been a volunteer at the local animal shelter for three months. Every weekend, I help take care of the dogs there. Some of them were found on the streets and are still getting used to people. My most important task is to walk the dogs and clean their cages. The shelter needs donations to buy food and medicine for these animals. Last month, we organized a charity event to collect pocket money from visitors. Most of all, I enjoy seeing the dogs become more active and friendly. One of the dogs, a brown one named Max, used to bark all the time. Now he loves to play with people. I feel happy knowing my small effort can make a difference in their lives.

title: 肯尼亚的村庄变化
passage: My grandfather, a Kenyan farmer, has lived in his village for over 60 years. Twenty years ago, he became good friends with a manager who visited the village for business. They haven't seen each other for ages! The manager recently returned and was amazed by the changes. The village now has a new hospital, which used to be a small building. Many young people used to work in big cities, but now more have come back to live and work here. The government has built a new highway linking the village to the capital. Digital payment systems have made business transactions convenient. My grandfather's farm has also changed - he now uses high-tech greenhouses to grow corn instead of traditional farmland. The manager commented that these changes have greatly improved life in the village.
passageZh: 我的祖父是一位肯尼亚农民，已经在他的村庄生活了60多年。20年前，他认识了一位来村里做生意的经理，他们成为了好朋友。他们已经很多年没有见面了！最近这位经理回来了，对村庄的变化感到惊讶。村里现在有了一家新医院，过去那只是一座小建筑。许多年轻人过去在大城市工作，但现在更多人已经回来在这里生活和工作。政府修建了一条连接村庄和首都的新公路。电子支付系统使商业交易变得方便。我祖父的农场也发生了变化——他现在使用高科技温室种植玉米，而不是传统的耕地。经理评论说这些变化极大地改善了村庄的生活。

title: 贝聿铭的建筑传奇
passage:
I. M. Pei was a world-famous British architect who created many amazing buildings around the globe. Born in China during the 20th century, he later moved to the United States where he established his own design company. Pei's work is known for its perfect balance between modern styles and traditional elements. Above all, what makes him truly admirable is his courage to try new ideas while respecting history.

One of his most famous projects is the glass pyramid at the Louvre Museum in Paris. It was difficult for many people to accept such a modern design next to the historic palace at first. However, Pei believed that good design could connect different centuries. Today, millions of visitors admire his creation every year. Pei once said that architecture should serve mankind and continue to inspire future generations. His buildings will live on as testaments to his vision and talent.
passageZh:
贝聿铭是一位世界著名的英国建筑师，在全球设计了众多令人惊叹的建筑。他出生于20世纪的中国，后来移居美国并建立了自己的设计公司。贝聿铭的作品以其现代风格与传统元素的完美平衡而闻名。最重要的是，他真正令人钦佩的是他有勇气尝试新想法的同时尊重历史。

他最著名的项目之一是巴黎卢浮宫的玻璃金字塔。起初，许多人很难接受这种现代设计紧邻历史宫殿。然而，贝聿铭相信好的设计可以连接不同的世纪。如今，每年有数百万游客欣赏他的作品。贝聿铭曾经说过，建筑应该为人类服务，并继续激励后代。他的建筑将继续作为他远见和才能的见证而存在。

title: 智能学习方法
passage: Li Hua, a ninth-grade student, was struggling with his English studies recently. He found it difficult to remember new words and improve his pronunciation. His English teacher suggested that he try some smart learning methods. In addition to using traditional textbooks, Li Hua started using e-books and podcasts to listen to native speakers. He created flashcards to help him build up his vocabulary step by step. Every evening, he would spend 30 minutes reading English magazines aloud to improve his pronunciation. Li Hua also discovered that looking up new words in an online dictionary was more efficient than using a printed one. His teacher gave him helpful feedback on his progress. After two months of actively trying these new methods, Li Hua's English skills improved significantly. He believes that finding enjoyable ways to learn is the key to success.

The geology of Mars is mysterious and full of surprises. Every night, I would look at the stars and wonder if there are other human beings beyond our solar system. passage: Last weekend, I attended a music festival in our city. As a music lover, I was excited to see different performances. The first piece I heard was classical music played by a talented pianist. Her fingers moved flowing across the keyboard, creating beautiful sounds.
